At Shutterfly, we make life's experiences unforgettable. We believe there is extraordinary power in the self-expression. That's why our family of brands helps customers create products and capture moments that reflect who they uniquely are.

The Sr. Director of Business Systems will report to the CIO and is responsible for overseeing all aspects of Shutterfly's business application landscape, including ERP, Finance and Supply Chain systems. Extensive experience with the SAP ecosystem is a requirement, including but not limited to S/4HANA, BASIS, PO, GRC, ECP, IBP, SF, WM, RISE, Ariba, SAC and Concur. The leader will need to help define and oversee the implementation of best-in-class business system standards, architecture and processes to maximize efficiency, productivity, availability and value across many business segments.

The Sr. Director of Business Systems must have solid leadership experience and excellent verbal and writing communication skills. Along with the CIO, the leader will need to proactively plan and align a Shutterfly specific business systems roadmaps. This position will be responsible for managing; People, projects, day-to-day support, budgets, multiple MSPs and ensure efficient business systems processes are maintained and followed to meet key business objectives. Understanding and utilizing the latest AI technologies within the business systems landscape is a must. Defining and establishing key metrics, KPI's and driving continual improvement based on this data is imperative.

Requirements:

* Perform personnel management tasks including but not limited to staff hiring, performance reviews, employee career development, etc.
* Work with other IT managers, business leaders, stakeholders and staff across multiple offices and time zones
* Continually align and communicate with business stakeholders
* Must have experience with software license rationalization
* Must be customer oriented with a strong grasp of the internal customer concept
* Adaptable to change and comfortable driving change management
* Experience working with all levels of employees from individual contributors all the way up to senior executives
* Develop and maintain processes and procedures to ensure business systems are highly productive for our employees and drive value for the overall business
* Work with external vendors, including but not limited to, SAP
* Must have extensive experience managing outsourced MSPs
* Experience working in manufacturing and or an e-commerce business highly desirable
* Familiarity with automation and AI technologies required
* Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (CS) or Management of Information Systems (MIS) is preferred
* Masters in a technical discipline and or an MBA is a plus
* 10+ years' experience in corporate business systems preferred
* 5-10 years' management and strategic experience preferred

Supporting a diverse and inclusive workforce is important to Shutterfly not only because it directly reflects our value

The Estate Lawyers is a growing estate planning and administration firm built on a simple belief: families deserve clear guidance and exceptional service during some of the most important moments of their lives. We take that seriously — in how we practice law, how we treat each other, and how we build our firm.

We operate on EOS (Entrepreneurial Operating System), which means we run on clear priorities, honest conversations, and measurable results. Our core values aren't wall décor — they show up in how we make decisions, how we hold each other accountable, and who we hire.

We're at an inflection point. The firm is growing — in clients, in people, and in locations — and we need the operational foundation to match. That's why this role exists.

**ABOUT THIS ROLE**

This is a builder role for a firm that is ready to scale.

As Director of Operations & Technology, you own the roadmap for how this firm grows — operationally, technologically, and structurally. You identify what's holding us back before it becomes a problem, design the fix, and see it through to measurable results.

You sit on the Leadership Team and report directly to the CEO/Integrator. You're not here to coordinate for other leaders — you're here to raise the standard of how the whole firm operates, and you have the authority to do it.

This role is right for someone who wants real accountability, not just responsibility. You will assess, prioritize, build, and measure. If something isn't working, you'll say so — and fix it.

You're drawn to complexity, not intimidated by it. You see operational gaps as problems worth solving, not someone else's mess to manage.

You set a high bar — for yourself and for the work around you. You don't need consensus to move, but you know how to bring people with you. You communicate directly and earn trust through follow-through, not charm.

The Linux Foundation is a 501(c)(6) non-profit that provides a neutral, trusted hub for developers and organizations to code, manage, and scale open technology projects and ecosystems.

UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.  
  
Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.  
  
UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

**About the role**
------------------

We're looking for a Director of Mission Operations to build and lead the team that delivers UFORCE's uncrewed systems missions. You'll own the operational portfolio across the customer lifecycle: pre-sale demonstrations, events and exercises, as well as post-sale deployments and customer implementations.

Reporting to the VP of Delivery, you'll lead and develop our Mission Managers, establish the standards and decision-making practices for safe, repeatable execution, and make sure concurrent missions have the people, equipment and support they need. You'll work closely with the Director of Training, who provides training personnel, pilots and field deployment engineers, and the Director of Operations, who supplies equipment, products and logistics.

This is a hands-on leadership role, but not one where you'll personally run every mission. You'll deploy when it matters—on first-of-kind, high-risk or high-visibility missions, or to coach and assess your team—while building an operation that succeeds through capable mission leaders.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Own the mission portfolio across demonstrations, exercises, deployments and customer implementations. Maintain a clear view of upcoming work, mission ownership, staffing, assets, readiness and risk.
* Review new opportunities for operational feasibility, capacity and risk before commitments are made. Resolve competing demands where you can, and bring recommended trade-offs to leadership when needed.
* Lead, hire and develop Mission Managers. Establish clear expectations, a structured qualification path, regular feedback and backup coverage, while managing deployment tempo and fatigue.
* Set and maintain practical mission standards, including planning templates, risk assessments, readiness reviews, briefs, communications plans and closeout reports. Check that they work in the field and improve them as the team learns.
* Establish clear decision and escalation boundaries with leadership and the appropriate technical and safety owners. Make it safe and expected for the team to raise concerns and pause or stop a mission.
* Work with the Director of Training to secure qualified personnel and with the Director of Operations to secure platforms, equipment, logistics and support. Set clear requirements and lead assigned personnel during mission execution

Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. The Senior Director of Production serves as AEG's on-site representative providing strategic leadership for the operational and execution of large-scale touring productions. Serving as the senior production representative on assigned tours, this role oversees daily show operations, revenue optimization, and cross-functional coordination to maximize tour performance. The Senior Director partners with artists, promoters, venue personnel, ticketing, and production teams to drive operational excellence while ensuring accurate execution throughout the tour lifecycle.

- Lead the day-to-day operational and financial execution of assigned touring productions, serving as the senior production representative with responsibility for production delivery, show settlements, and operational decision-making.

- Oversee daily financial settlements, expense management, and accounting activities, ensuring timely reconciliation and compliance with internal financial controls and contractual requirements.
- Coordinate cross-functional tour operations by partnering with ticketing, venue management, production, catering, temporary staffing, and other internal and external stakeholders to ensure seamless show execution.
- Provide subject matter expertise and operational leadership by developing best practices, mentoring production staff, and supporting organizational initiatives related to tour operations, financial processes, and production standards.

Required Qualifications:
- Extensive experience managing large-scale touring productions, including live event operations and financial settlements.
- Strong knowledge of production accounting, revenue management, and ticketing operations.

Alpha-9 Oncology is seeking a Director, Program Management to join the clinical team to drive planning and execution across our radiopharmaceutical pipeline. Our programs target solid and hematologic malignancies, and with clinical studies now underway, this role brings the structure that keeps programs on time, in scope, and within budget.

Working alongside our program leads and functional experts, you’ll build and own the integrated plans that connect Clinical, Regulatory, CMC, and nonclinical teams. Program strategy and clinical decisions sit with the program leads. Your role is to frame the options, balance quality, speed, and cost, and guide the team to clear decisions, then make sure those decisions are carried through. - Build program timelines and scenarios, mapping the dependencies specific to RLT, such as isotope supply, drug product manufacturing, and imaging agent availability.
- Act as the team’s point person on program risk, identifying issues early and driving mitigation and contingency plans with functional leads.
- Present program status, trade-offs, and options to program leads and the leadership team to support timely decisions.
- Coordinate cross-functional inputs for key milestones, including IND and CTA filings, study starts, and data readouts.
- Run program team meetings, owning agendas, decision logs, and follow-through on action items.
- Establish the program management tools, templates, and processes that scale with the company.
- Manage program budgets and forecasts in partnership with Finance and functional leads.
- Track deliverables from CROs, CDMOs, and isotope suppliers against the program plan, and escalate when their timelines put milestones at risk.
- Connect nonclinical, CMC, regulatory, and clinical plans as programs move from IND-enabling work into the clinic.

- Bachelor's degree in a scientific or related field with 10+ years of biotech or pharmaceutical experience, or an advanced degree with 7+ years of experience, including at least 5 years in drug development program or project management.
- Advanced degree in life sciences, MBA, or PMP certification preferred.
- Strong understanding of the drug development lifecycle and the interdependencies across Clinical, Regulatory, CMC, and Nonclinical functions.

About Amyris

Amyris uses its biomanufacturing platform to transform industries to renewable biological chemistry, with operations in the United States and Brazil. Its Computing organization empowers, improves, and innovates computational, data, and technology systems across Amyris to achieve operational excellence, supporting a unique mix of SaaS, custom software, and AI capabilities powering enterprise, R&D pipeline, and manufacturing operations.

Position Overview

The IT Director is a technical leader accountable for the engineering, reliability, and operation of Amyris’s global IT infrastructure across networks, servers, endpoints, cybersecurity, knowledge management, and the service desk. The role combines hands-on technical leadership with leadership of internal IT teams and MSPs in the United States and Brazil, partnering across Computing and the enterprise to maintain and advance the infrastructure upon which our SaaS and custom platforms rely.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on DevOps leader (CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, containerization, observability) with enterprise architecture experience across networking, identity, security, databases, and infrastructure. They turn ambiguous demands into well-defined, automated, and documented solutions. The role keeps regular overlap with both US Pacific and Brazil working hours.

Location : Hybrid in Emeryville, CA.

greenhouse:anduril industries:5280931007.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The duty of this organization is to enable our Customers' ongoing Mission Readiness. From the moment they say "go" until the contract is fulfilled. We are only successful when the customer's mission is successful.

Mission Readiness is the post-production shared services organization for Anduril. This team supports the Business Lines and Divisions throughout the lifecycle of their product, from initial sustainment concept through delivery, installation, operation, repair and return. These service offerings also include providing technical publications, training, customer support, connectivity services and other value-added services. To the degree the Business elects, we accept the delegated responsibility for upfront and continued delivery of the committed service solutions. This team endeavors to provide the Business Lines, as our internal customers, shared mission services that are more efficient and cost effective than if they chose to provide them directly. By offering mission support capabilities and capacity that are not "core" to the Business, the Business can focus resources on addressing the next big need while we ensure existing commitments are met.

As Anduril's installed base grows across an increasing number of products and Business Lines, our MRO organization needs to move from a collection of program-specific repair processes and tools to a hardened, scalable operating model. This role is about leading that shift.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Director of MRO Transformation to lead the modernization and scaling of Anduril's repair operations. Where our Head of MRO oversees the collective repair function, this Director role owns the transformation agenda: establishing core processes for any Business Line to leverage, selecting and implementing the tools and systems MRO runs on, and driving the change management needed to get a fast-growing collection of programs onto common, scalable rails. You will assess where today's pockets of good activity exist, build the roadmap to modernize them, and lead cross-functional teams through the change without slowing down repair turnaround for products already in the field. This is a build-the-plane-while-flying role for someone who has led operational or digital

Mavericks Wanted

When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on

In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare disease, and develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible.

About the role

Chime's Data Science & Machine Learning team powers decisions across the company, from how we protect members to how we build products for them. We're looking for a Director to lead that team through its biggest shift yet: moving from traditional models to a modern, AI-driven approach built on transformers and foundation models. You'll lead managers and staff-level engineers, define what great ML looks like at Chime's scale, and rebuild the practice around it. If you want to shape the future of ML at a company where it directly affects members' financial lives, this is the role.

In this role, you can expect to
- Lead and grow Chime's ML organization, managing managers and staff-level engineers across all of Chime's ML work.
- Set the vision and roadmap for moving Chime's models from traditional approaches to transformer- and foundation-model-based systems.
- Coach your managers to build strong, high-performing teams, and raise the technical bar across the practice.
- Shape the architecture of Chime's ML platform, including how we train, fine-tune, serve and scale models on a modern GPU-based stack.
- Define what good ML looks like at Chime: standards for model development, evaluation, deployment and monitoring.
- Partner with product, engineering, risk and business leaders to turn ML into measurable impact for members.
- Make the call on when to build, buy or fine-tune, and explain the trade-offs clearly to executives.

To thrive in this role, you have
- Deep machine learning expertise, with a well-formed point of view on transformer and foundation models and where they do (and don't) beat traditional approaches.
- Familiarity with GPUs and the modern ML stack, from training and fine-tuning to serving models in production at scale.
- Experience managing managers and staff-level ICs, with the technical credibility to earn their trust.
- A track record of building or transforming an ML practice: hiring, setting standards and growing leaders.
- Experience setting a multi-year ML strategy and turning it into shipped results.
- Clear communication with executives and cross-functional partners; you can make complex ML trade-offs easy to follow.
- Bonus: experience applying ML in fintech or another regulated industry.

Data Engineering sits at the heart of Chime: nearly every product, analytics and AI initiative runs through the data our teams build. As a Director of Engineering, you'll lead Data Foundations and Insights, managing engineering managers and staff engineers who build the foundations the rest of Chime depends on. About the Team

Customer Engineering & Success is where CircleCI’s customer relationships are won, deepened, and renewed. The organization brings together the technical teams that help customers succeed with CircleCI at every stage, from the first proof-of-concept through enterprise-wide adoption and long-term partnership. It includes four groups:
- Field Engineering , which partners with Sales on technical discovery, solution design, and proofs-of-concept, and advises high-touch accounts after the sale.
- Technical Success Management , which guides strategic, enterprise, and commercial customers to adoption, value, and expansion.
- Digital Customer Success , which serves SMB customers through a scaled, data-driven engagement model.
- Support Engineering , which resolves complex technical issues for customers around the world, around the clock.

The team works across North America, Europe, and Japan and serves engineering organizations at companies of every size. CircleCI processes more than a million builds a day, so this team sees how the world’s best engineering teams ship software. It turns that insight into better outcomes for customers and a stronger product. Its work drives retention, expansion, and revenue directly.

About the Role

Reporting to the Chief Revenue Officer, the VP of Customer Engineering & Success leads CircleCI’s full technical customer journey, from pre-sales technical wins through adoption, support, renewal, and expansion. You’ll unite field engineering, technical success, digital success, and support engineering into one connected motion, so customers get a consistent and expert experience no matter how they engage with us.

Success in this role means higher net revenue retention, lower churn, faster time-to-value, and stronger technical win rates. It also means an organization that scales efficiently through the right mix of high-touch, pooled, and digital engagement. You’ll be the voice of the customer at the executive table and shape product priorities, go-to-market strategy, and the annual plan with insight drawn directly from how customers use CircleCI.

What You’ll Do:
- Set the vision, strategy, and operating model for a global organization spanning Field Engineering, Technical Success Management, Digital Customer Success, and Support Engineering, and integrate pre-sales and post-sales technical engagement into one seamless customer journey.
- Own retention and expansion outcomes, including gross and net revenue retention, churn reduction, and adoption, and partner with Sales leadership to drive technical wins and land-and-expand growth.
- Build a coverage model that matches customer segment to engagement type (high-touch, pooled, and digital/scaled), and use data and automation to scale efficiently as the customer base grows.

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Recruitment Fraud Alert

We’ve learned that scammers are impersonating Commvault team members—including HR and leadership—via email or text. These bad actors may conduct fake interviews and ask for personal information, such as your social security number.

What to know:
- Commvault does  not  conduct interviews by email or text.
- We will never ask you to submit sensitive documents (including banking information, SSN, etc) before your first day.
- Commvault recruiters may contact prospective candidates through LinkedIn and other professional networking platforms regarding career opportunities. If you are unsure whether a recruiting communication is legitimate, review the profile to ensure they have a badge verifying them as a Commvault employee.

If you suspect a recruiting scam, please contact us at wwrecruitingteam@commvault.com

About Commvault

Commvault (NASDAQ: CVLT) delivers continuous recovery for the AI era. We help organizations stay ready for constant disruption by returning critical data, applications, identities, and AI systems to a clean, trusted state. Our purpose-built recovery solutions span cloud-native and hybrid environments, leveraging AI to enable resilience at enterprise scale.

Commvault is seeking a  Head of Global Systems Integrator Alliances to lead and scale one of our most strategic routes to market.

This executive will own Commvault's global strategy, business performance and executive relationships across our Global Systems Integrator ecosystem. The mandate is clear: turn strategic partnerships into partner-led offerings, qualified pipeline, recurring revenue, new customers and meaningful services opportunities for our partners .

This is not a traditional alliance-management role. We are building an offerings-led growth engine where Commvault becomes a foundational component of the cyber resilience, cloud, identity, AI and managed services solutions that leading GSIs take to market. Our strategy is moving from having partners sell our technology to having partners build, deliver and operate differentiated customer offerings powered by Commvault .

Commvault provides enterprise resilience across hybrid, cloud-native and AI environments, bringing together security, identity and recovery capabilities while extending cloud-native protection through Clumio by Commvault.

What You'll Do

Build and Scale the Global GSI Business
- Define and execute Commvault's global GSI strategy across priority partners, markets and industries.
- Own partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue performance.
- Establish multi-year joint business plans with measurable commitments around growth, co-build offerings, practices, enablement and investment.
- Build executive-level relationships across leading global systems integrators.

Who is Credible?

Credible is a leading U.S. consumer finance marketplace, transforming the way consumers access and compare financial products. We operate at a consumer and enterprise level. On the consumer side, we help millions of people make smarter financial decisions by comparing personalized, pre-qualified offers across student loans, personal loans, mortgages, credit cards, and insurance — all without impacting their credit score. On the enterprise side, we power financial product comparison and distribution through deep integrations and partnerships with lenders, insurance carriers, and financial institutions, as well as providing marketplace technology and capabilities to third-party partners and distribution channels.

Credible is looking for a motivated, experienced Director of Architecture and Infrastructure to join our growing team. This is a remote, player-coach leadership role reporting to the SVP of Technology.

You will directly lead two platform teams of four engineers each, the foundation that every Credible customer- and partner-facing application runs on:

• Infrastructure Platform (DevOps): infrastructure, AWS, Kubernetes, CI/CD processes, and the internally developed applications that support them. This team works primarily in Golang.

• Application Platform: the shared services and libraries used across our customer- and partner-facing applications, primarily written in Ruby. Examples include authentication, user disclosures, logging, integrations with SaaS products (such as email marketing systems), Kafka tooling, and GraphQL API tooling.

You will also partner with other engineering teams during the architecture and design phase of larger projects, and help advance how we approach architecture and design review across the broader engineering organization. Your work will sit closely alongside our Security team.

This role is posted at the Director level; an exceptionally qualified candidate may be hired at the Senior Director level.

Responsibilities

• Lead, mentor, and grow the Infrastructure Platform and Application Platform teams; hire well, set clear expectations, and develop future leaders

• Make stability the first priority: drive reliability, resilience, and operational excellence across our infrastructure and shared services

• Bring a security mindset to every decision, working in close partnership with our Security Director and team

• Support SOC 2 and SOX compliance through well-designed controls, processes, and tooling

• Own the on-call rotation for the Infrastructure Platform team, ensuring it is sustainable, well-documented, and continuously improving

• Provide architecture and design guidance on larger projects, partnering with other engineering teams in the design phase and leading design reviews

• Help evolve our architecture and design review process across the engineering organization

• Guide our microservices architecture, including the thoughtful decomposition of remaining larg

Every product Databricks ships has to be priced, contracted, rated and billed before it can earn a dollar. greenhouse:fivetran:8196773003.description:
From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.

Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.

During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

We are looking for a Global Head of Deal Strategy and Operations to lead the worldwide deal function for a rapidly scaling data and analytics business formed by the combination of Fivetran and dbt Labs. This is a commercial strategy role as much as an operational one with a mandate to make our deals bigger, better, and faster. The leader owns the deal structures, pricing inputs, policies, and governance that drive more revenue and higher ASP, cleaner and lower-risk terms, and real velocity across every region and segment, while de-risking the business.

This is a pivotal role at a pivotal moment. The business is integrating two commercial engines, two product portfolios, and two sets of systems into a single combined go-to-market. The role sets the strategy for how deals get structured, priced, routed, reviewed, and approved, and acts as a key commercial advisor to GTM leadership on the structures that drive growth, including ELA and commercial strategy, cross-sell, and new product launches. It leads a global team across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC and partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Product, Systems, Pricing, and Partner Marketplace to keep decisions fast, consistent, and scalable.

This leader is an equal part strategist, operator, and trusted business partner. The ideal ca

About Pioneering Intelligence

Pioneering Intelligence develops AI capabilities for the Flagship Pioneering ecosystem, including novel architectures of generative models, simulation, and AI reasoning systems. We unify and accelerate the AI innovation of Flagship’s integrated model of science, entrepreneurship, and capital.

The Role

Pioneering Intelligence is building a growing portfolio of tools, apps and agentic systems on shared capabilities in data, models and agents. We are seeking a Senior Director, Platform Experience to turn that portfolio into one platform that scientists trust and adopt. You will set the experience vision and architecture for the platform, define how scientists work with AI agents, and build the design system that teams across PI and the Flagship ecosystem ship with.

You will report to the VP of Platform for Pioneering Intelligence. You will work every day with product managers, engineers, ML researchers, computational biologists and the scientists who use PI’s tools, and you will be design’s voice to PI leadership.

This is a hands-on role. You will personally design and ship the scientific workflows that define the platform, from research and early concepts through coded prototypes, production UI and QA. You will also shape how design works inside an AI-driven development lifecycle, choosing and evolving the AI-assisted tools that connect design intent with working software.

- Set the experience vision and architecture for PI’s platform
- Define how scientists work with AI agents
- Personally design and ship end-to-end scientific workflows
- Develop a coded design system used across PI and the Flagship ecosystem
- Build design into an AI-driven development lifecycle

- Designing for scientists or other technical experts. You’ve designed for life-sciences R&D, working directly with researchers and scientists. We will also consider experience in another technically complex domain if you can show you get up to speed fast in new areas.
- Building a design system in code. You’ve built a design system and pattern library in code that multiple teams adopted.

greenhouse:flex:4750380005.description:
Flex is a growth-stage, NYC headquartered FinTech company that is building the payment layer for life's financial obligations, giving households one place to see, split, and pay their bills around how they live and get paid. By offering greater choice over how and when payments are made and allowing eligible on time payments to help build a positive credit history, Flex puts households back in control of their cash flow.

That work brings together people with different perspectives who challenge the status quo and take ownership of solving difficult problems. For you, that means doing the best work of your career next to people who make you better, and together bringing ideas to life that make a real impact for the people we serve.

About the Role

We are seeking a strategic leader who pairs deep systems expertise with strong process design instincts to build and own Flex's Financial Systems & Transformation function from the ground up. This is a rare opportunity to define a new pillar within the Finance organization at a fast-scaling fintech — one where the scope extends well beyond traditional ERP administration into agentic AI infrastructure, process automation, and the controls architecture that will underpin Flex’s next phase of growth.

As Director, Financial Systems & Transformation, you will own the internal financial systems that power Flex’s accounting and financial reporting function — including our core ERP, procure-to-pay (P2P), T&E systems, and additional financial reporting tooling as the function matures. General Atlantic is a leading global investor with more than four and a half decades of experience providing capital and strategic support for over 885 companies throughout its history. As the Director, Off-Planet Programs you will own and lead ICON’s off-planet robotics, construction, and materials initiatives across hardware, electrical, software, material science, R&D, and operations. This is a highly strategic and execution-driven leadership role, partnering closely with program management, executive leadership, and external stakeholders to scale ICON’s space robotics and extraterrestrial construction capabilities.

You will shape the long-term technical vision, infrastructure, and execution strategy for ICON’s off-planet programs—driving innovation, operational excellence, and sustained market leadership in autonomous construction beyond Earth.

This is a full-time position based on-site on ICON's Austin, TX HQ Campus.

ICON builds robotic systems that construct multi-story buildings. The company launched Titan commercially in March 2026, has raised over $550M, and holds more than $360M in government contracts across the Army, Air Force, DARPA, and NASA. That growth means more printers in the field, more sites running concurrently, and a larger installed base that has to stay productive.

This role owns Engineering Services: the team that keeps ICON’s printer fleet and site equipment reliable, supportable, and current. That includes sustaining engineering, engineering change management, reliability and root-cause analysis, and the technical content field and operations teams run on. New product design stays with Hardware Engineering; Engineering Services owns everything after release.

You will report to the VP, Operations Technology and work daily with Hardware Engineering, Construction Operations, Field Service, Supply Chain, and Quality. You are accountable for fleet uptime, change velocity, and building the service engineering function to match a growing installed base.

Responsibilities

Fleet Reliability & Sustaining Engineering
- Own reliability performance across deployed Vulcan, Phoenix, and Titan systems; set uptime and MTBF targets with Operations and report against them.
- Run root-cause analysis on recurring field failures and drive corrective designs through to release and fleet retrofit.
- Prioritize and manage the sustaining backlog against site schedules, parts availability, and cost.

Engineering Change & Configuration Management
- Own the ECO process end to end, including impact assessment, approval, documentation, and rollout to units in the field.
- Maintain as-built configuration control across the fleet so Operations, Supply Chain, and Service know exactly what is deployed where.

Service Readiness & Technical Enablement
- Deliver the service manuals, procedures, training content, and diagnostic tools that technicians and site crews depend on.
- Define spares strategy and serviceability requirements with Supply Chain and feed them back into new product programs.

Team Leadership
- Lead and grow a team of engineers and managers; set priorities, develop people, and manage the department budget.
- Represent Engineering Services in cross-functional planning with Hardware, Operations, and Prime program leadership.

Required Qualifications
- 10+ years in mechanical, electromechanical, or systems engineering, including 5+ years leading engineering teams.
- Experience owning sustaining engineering, reliability, or service engineering for complex deployed hardware (heavy equipment, robotics, industrial machinery, or similar).
- Hands-on experience running engineering change and configuration management processes.
- Track record of leading root-cause investigations and driving corrective actions to closure.
- Based in or willing to relocate to Austin, TX; this role is on site.

Description

Keeper Security is hiring a Director of IT Operations to lead our global enterprise IT function. This role will oversee IT infrastructure, end-user support, identity lifecycle management, IT service management, business continuity, vendor relationships and IT operations for Keeper’s distributed workforce. This is a 100% remote position, with the opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates based in the El Dorado Hills, CA or Chicago, IL metro area.

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and is sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help build the systems and processes that enable our global workforce to work securely and efficiently.

About Keeper

Keeper Security is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity software companies that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in over 150 countries. Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com .

About the Job

This role will lead the strategy, operations and continuous improvement of Keeper’s corporate IT environment. The ideal candidate is an experienced IT leader who combines strong operational discipline with a customer-focused mindset and the ability to build scalable systems for a growing, distributed workforce.

The Director of IT Operations will be responsible for developing a multi-year IT roadmap, leading the IT Operations team, managing the IT operating budget and ensuring that employees have secure and reliable access to the tools and systems they need to be successful.

Responsibilities

The datasets power our computational models, which leads to better drug designs, creating a flywheel that gets stronger with every campaign. Netskope (NASDAQ: NTSK) is a leader in modern security and networking for the cloud and AI era. We secure and accelerate cloud, data, and AI in real time, everywhere. Thousands of customers, including more than 30 of the Fortune 100, trust the Netskope One platform, its Zero Trust Engine, and the powerful NewEdge network to gain full visibility and control without performance trade-offs.

At Netskope, our technology is driven by our greatest strength: our people. We believe that belonging powers innovation, and success is both personal and organizational. In this executive role, you will oversee high-throughput, low-latency network infrastructure, multi-region cloud and edge data center environments, customer support, and round-the-clock Network Operations (NOC/SOC). You will ensure carrier-grade availability, sub-millisecond packet inspection performance, and bulletproof operational resilience against massive, distributed cyber threats.

- Security & Compliance: Partner with internal CISO/InfoSec teams to ensure operational infrastructure complies with FedRAMP, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and Zero Trust security architectures.

Nextdoor is the essential neighborhood network. Neighbors, public agencies, and businesses use Nextdoor to connect around local information that matters in more than 350,000 neighborhoods across 11 countries. Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

Within the Product Security team, our Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) owns Okta's response when a security vulnerability in our products is reported, exploited, or puts customers at risk, across Okta, Auth0 and the systems they run on. PSIRT triages reports from researchers, customers, our bug bounty program and our own automated discovery, leads each incident from intake to closure, drives fixes with engineering and leadership, and publishes CVEs and security advisories as Okta's CVE Numbering Authority.

AI is changing how vulnerabilities are found, by us and by attackers, and the volume of high-impact reports is rising quickly. We seek a director to lead PSIRT through that change: run day-to-day incident response, build the team and the agentic workflows that let it scale, and be the steady, credible voice for Okta when a vulnerability matters to our customers.

What You Will Do
- Lead Okta's PSIRT program across all business units, defining its strategy, roadmap and operating model
- Own the vulnerability-handling lifecycle, from intake and triage through remediation, coordinated disclosure and post-incident review, and keep our procedures and runbooks current
- Act as senior incident lead on Critical and high-profile vulnerabilities, including industry-wide issues, and make clear calls under pressure
- Partner with Engineering leaders to drive fixes and hotfixes on time, while engineering owns remediation
- Run coordinated disclosure with researchers and partners, and own Okta's CVE and security advisory process with Customer Trust and Security Communications
- Work closely with Cyber Defense, Identity Defense, Legal and Federal teams on exploitation analysis, customer impact and regulatory obligations
- Own the bug bounty program and relationships with the security research community

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

Job overview:

The Eligibility & Revenue Systems are the enterprise backbone that makes the employer and health plan business work: they ingest files, determine eligibility, power billing, and integrate incentives so customers can get members into care without friction.  Together they cover Omada's part of the employer and health plan revenue cycle: file ingestion and partner integrations, eligibility, and claims and invoicing.

greenhouse:psiquantum:8184378003.description:
PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we now have the funding, the government validation, and the sites under construction to make it real.

SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the team

The IT team supports SambaNova’s employees and infrastructure. We manage the servers, networks, and cloud accounts our engineering teams use to build and test AI chips and systems. We also handle employee laptops, accounts, and software, and we run security across the company. The team is small and works closely with engineering and DevOps.

About the role

As Director of IT on the IT team, you will lead infrastructure, end-user IT, security operations, and DevOps support across the company. You will set the direction for the function and grow the team, and you will also do hands-on work when the team needs it. This role can be leveled at Director or Senior Director depending on experience.

Responsibilities
- Lead server and backend infrastructure, including on-prem and cloud systems, networking, storage, and identity
- Run desktop and end-user IT, including laptop provisioning, SaaS tools, help desk, and onboarding and off boarding
- Build and run the security program and security operations, including endpoint protection, access control, monitoring, and incident response
- Partner with engineering on DevOps tooling, CI/CD infrastructure, and automation
- Hire and manage the IT team, and set its roadmap and budget
- Manage vendors and contracts for IT and security tools
- Configure systems, troubleshoot outages, and write automation yourself when needed

Required qualifications
- B.S. in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field
- 10+ years of experience in IT infrastructure and operations
- 5+ years of experience leading IT teams
- Experience running both backend infrastructure and end-user IT
- Experience building or running a security operations program
- Experience with DevOps tools such as Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines
- Hands-on experience with Linux, Windows, and macOS administration, identity management such as Okta or Entra ID, and MDM
- Able to work onsite at our Bay Area office on a regular basis

Preferred qualifications
- Experience at a startup or high-growth company
- Experience supporting hardware or semiconductor engineering teams, including HPC or lab environments
- Experience with SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar compliance programs
- Experience scaling an IT team through rapid headcount growth

At SolarWinds, we’re a people-first company. Our purpose is to enrich the lives of the people we serve—including our employees, customers, shareholders, partners, and communities. Join us in our mission to help customers accelerate business transformation with simple, powerful, and secure solutions.

The ideal candidate thrives in an innovative, fast-paced environment and is collaborative, accountable, ready, and empathetic. We’re looking for individuals who believe they can accomplish more as a team and create lasting growth for themselves and others. We hire based on attitude, competency, and commitment. Solarians are ready to advance our world-class solutions in a fast-paced environment and accept the challenge to lead with purpose. If you’re looking to build your career with an exceptional team, you’ve come to the right place. Join SolarWinds and grow with us!

What you will do

SolarWinds is looking for a Director of Product Security to build and lead a new, AI-first product security team for our SaaS portfolio: SolarWinds Observability, SolarWinds Service Desk, SolarWinds Incident Response, Pingdom, Loggly, Papertrail and Database Performance Monitor. The team owns security from incident response through prevention. That covers how security findings are triaged and routed, SaaS security incident command, software supply chain and build integrity, application, AI and cloud security standards, and the engineering evidence behind our SOC 2 and FedRAMP programs.
- This team is AI-first. Its engineers build the agents that do the routine work, such as triaging findings, opening fixes, reviewing code and collecting audit evidence, and they make the judgment calls themselves.
- Build and lead a team of security engineers across the US, Europe and India, starting with the first set of hires and growing it based on measured results.
- Set the product security strategy and standards for our SaaS products, and co-chair the Product Security Council with engineering leadership.
- Own SaaS security incident command, working with the CISO organization.
- Own how security findings are triaged and routed to the teams that fix them, and publish a monthly report on critical and high risk across the portfolio.
- Lead the team's AI-first operating model: a budgeted set of security agents the team builds, measured by cost per outcome and by how often they miss real issues.
- Own software supply chain and build integrity standards across the portfolio for SaaS products.
- Agree clear boundaries and shared programs with the CISO organization to avoid duplicating its work.
- Get the most out of the security tools already selected, set requirements for them, and take part in tool consolidation or new tool decisions.
- Work with SRE and product teams to move SOC 2 and FedRAMP evidence collection from manual work to automation.
- Own the team's hiring plan, budget and token budget, and report progress to engineering leadership.

Required Qualifications
- 12+ years in

We're building healthcare tech for a system that desperately needs it.

Each year, millions of Americans deal with confusing changes to their Medicare plans that impact their prescriptions, access to care, and pocketbooks. These aren’t just inconveniences – they are potentially life-altering changes that leave seniors medically and financially vulnerable.

Independent Medicare advisors play a crucial role in guiding seniors through this complexity and helping them find the right coverage for their needs. But their ability to be effective healthcare advocates has long been hamstrung by broken tools and outdated systems.

Spark is fixing that. We’re the fastest-growing Medicare platform in the country, combining AI, an industry-leading CRM, and client services to transform how 10,000+ brokers acquire, enroll, and support clients in their local communities.

Join a talent-dense team from Square, Ramp, Yext, Oscar, and Cedar — backed by Primary Ventures and Viewpoint Ventures — that is serious about building technology to expand access to quality healthcare. Spark is looking for a Director of Software Engineering to lead engineering across our broker productivity product and core platform. You'll make sure our platform keeps up with a fast-growing customer base, and you'll keep our web-based broker platform sustainable as it scales.

Who We Are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the Team

The Solutions Architecture team partners with Stripe’s users to design and build transformative solutions that unlock growth, modernize business models, and shape the future of commerce. We work with executives, product leaders, and engineering teams at the world’s largest and most innovative companies, helping them translate ambitious strategies into scalable solutions on Stripe.

Strategic Accounts Solutions Architecture serves Stripe’s most complex and consequential users. The team combines deep technical expertise, commercial judgment, and customer empathy to solve problems that often have no established playbook. Its work not only helps individual users grow; it also surfaces emerging needs and opportunities that can inform Stripe’s product strategy and create value for users at global scale. These Solution Architects are deeply embedded in these users and are working along as their technical co-founders.

The Head of Strategic Accounts, Solutions Architecture will lead a team of senior architects who are trusted partners to strategic, key, and major accounts. This leader will set the vision for the team, develop exceptional technical talent, and work closely with account leadership to deepen and grow Stripe’s most important relationships. They will also build a strong partnership with Product and Engineering, turning insights from leading-edge customer engagements into the next wave of innovation across Stripe.

This is a highly technical, hands-on leadership role. The successful candidate will be comfortable moving between executive conversations, account strategy, architecture reviews, product discussions, and direct support for the team’s most complex engagements. They will be AI-enabled in how they lead and operate, highly curious about new technologies and business models, and committed to helping their team and Stripe continuously raise the bar.

- Set the vision, strategy, and operating model for Strategic Accounts Solutions Architecture, aligning the team’s priorities with Stripe’s user, product, and business objectives.

About Valar Atomics

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team

As part of the Engineering organization, Mechanical Engineering designs and develops the mechanical systems, components, and equipment that power Valar's advanced nuclear technologies. The team ensures designs are robust, manufacturable, and optimized for long-term performance .

The Role

Our TRISO fuel fabrication line turns U3O8 powder into finished TRISO compacts through three core process families: sol-gel kernel production, chemical vapor deposition (CVD) coating, and high-temperature furnace processing. Each runs on purpose-built process skids that our team designs, procures, builds, and commissions.

The Director of Fuel Equipment Engineering owns the design of that equipment end to end: from early skid design through to fabrication, factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, and handover to fuel production operations.

This role is a hands-on technical authority who understands chemical process equipment, fluidized-bed reactors, and high-temperature furnace systems at a deep level. It is also a team leader who builds and develops the equipment engineering organization as the fuel program scales.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership — Fuel Process Equipment
- Own the equipment design basis for the full TRISO fabrication flow, from U3O8 receipt through finished coated particle
- Oversee technical leads for each equipment family and guide the design and commissioning of that equipment
- Define skid architecture standards: modularity, materials of construction, containment and confinement, maintainability, and remote or glovebox operation where required
- Partner with process engineering to translate process recipes and critical parameters into equipment requirements that deliver repeatable kernel and coating quality
- Ensure equipment designs meet nuclear criticality safety, radiological protection, chemical hazard, and fire protection requirements

Equipment Design, Fabrication & Commissioning
- Lead equipment scope for development rigs, pilot lines, and production lines, from P&IDs and layouts through detailed mechanical design
- Own fabrication oversight, factory acceptance testing (FAT), site acceptance testing (SAT), and equipment commissioning
- Drive scale-up from laboratory and pilot equipment to production throughput while preserving product specifications
- Establish equipment relia

Voyager is an innovative defense, national security, and space technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets, leading in the race for technological and operational superiority from the ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers, and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt, and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers, and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person,  forge the future with Voyager.

The Executive Vice President, Engineering for Space, Defense, & National Security is responsible for leading and scaling the engineering organization to deliver high-quality, reliable products aligned with business goals and growth priorities.

The position reports to the President, Space, Defense & National Security and is based in the Long Beach, CA OR Denver Metro Area, CO area. This role is onsite.

Most engineering leaders inherit an organization.

You’ll invent one.

Right now, thousands of Voyager engineers are building things the country needs and the industry has never moved fast enough to deliver:
- Propulsion and electronics at scale , built to put real combat capability in the field for missile defense and Golden Dome
- Advanced weapon systems that protect warfighters and allies
- Lunar landers that carry NASA and commercial payloads to the surface of the Moon, with the Griffin program carrying the Astrobotic heritage
- Commercial LEO destinations , the stations where humanity will work, research, and manufacture in orbit
- Cislunar and Lagrange-point infrastructure , the next layer of habitats and logistics beyond Earth orbit
- Space-qualified systems and payloads with flight heritage on the most demanding platforms humans have built

That’s the portfolio today.

Now add what’s coming: new acquisitions. International operations. Allied partnerships. New domains and new customers. Every one of them needs an engineering backbone that doesn’t exist yet. You decide what it looks like, and then you build it.

Aerospace and defense takes years to go from idea to hardware. The country doesn’t have years.

We want days. Weeks.

At WelbeHealth, we serve our communities’ most vulnerable seniors through shared intention, pioneering spirit, and the courage to love. These core values and our participant focus lead the way no matter what.

The Director, IT Portfolio & Delivery provides leadership for enterprise technology portfolio planning, governance, delivery management, and performance visibility. Working closely with Technology leadership and business partners, this role translates strategy into an integrated portfolio of initiatives, establishes consistent delivery practices, and enables informed prioritization, sequencing, capacity, funding, and risk decisions.

This role is different because the Director, IT Portfolio & Delivery at WelbeHealth:
- Leads enterprise technology portfolio strategy, governance, and delivery, translating organizational priorities into an integrated roadmap of initiatives that drives business outcomes, optimizes resources, and supports WelbeHealth’s continued growth
- Builds and strengthens scalable delivery practices through data-driven decision-making, financial oversight, and cross-functional collaboration, ensuring technology investments are effectively prioritized, risks are proactively managed, and teams are equipped to deliver results

We care about our team members. That’s why we offer:
- Medical insurance coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
- Work/life balance - We mean it! 17 days of personal time off (PTO), 12 holidays observed annually, and 6 sick days
- 401K savings + match
- Comprehensive compensation package including base pay and bonus
- And additional benefits!

On the day-to-day, you will:
- Lead the enterprise Technology portfolio intake, assessment, prioritization, sequencing, and governance process, as well as translate Technology strategy and roadmaps into an integrated, executable portfolio with clear outcomes, milestones, dependencies, resource needs, and decision points
- Lead, coach, and develop Principal Scrum Masters and ITS Project Managers, including hiring, onboarding, goal setting, workload management, performance support, and succession planning, as well as assign delivery leadership based on initiative complexity, risk, methodology, and organizational priority
- Partner with Finance and Accounting teams to coordinate Technology capital expenditure planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and reconciliation
- Maintain a reliable portfolio view of approved capital investments, forecasted spend, actual spend, commitments, variances, and expected completion timing

- Assess current processes, identify root causes of friction or inconsistency, and lead cross-functional improvements that simplify work and strengthen accountability
- Build trusted relationships with executives, functional leaders, delivery teams, vendors, and other stakeholders, as well as manage

Yugabyte is the company behind YugabyteDB , the AI-ready, multi-modal, distributed PostgreSQL database for cloud-native apps. Trusted by industry leaders including Shopify, Paramount+, GM, Kroger, Fiserv, and NPCI, YugabyteDB has been deployed in over 100 countries and powers more than 5 million clusters worldwide.

Together, our hard-working team of experts and our industry-leading technology are uniquely positioned to meet the demands of modern workloads: geo-distributed, ultra-resilient, and built to scale without limits.

Our Yugabeings (distributed, like our database) span 12+ countries and multiple time zones, sharing expertise from diverse backgrounds and industries.

Yugabyte is the company behind YugabyteDB, the AI-ready, multi-modal, distributed PostgreSQL database for cloud-native apps. Trusted by industry leaders including Shopify, Paramount+, GM, Kroger, Fiserv, and NPCI, YugabyteDB has been deployed in over 100 countries and powers more than 5 million clusters worldwide.

Together, our hard-working team of experts and our industry-leading technology are uniquely positioned to meet the demands of modern workloads: geo-distributed, ultra-resilient, and built to scale without limits.

At Yugabyte, we are on a mission to build an open source, high-performance, distributed, and fault-tolerant PostgreSQL-compatible database for powering global, internet-scale applications. Our Database-as-a-Service (DBaaS) organization brings YugabyteDB to customers wherever they run: as a fully managed service on the major clouds with YugabyteDB Aeon, inside their own cloud accounts with Aeon BYOC, in their own data centers and Kubernetes environments with YugabyteDB Anywhere, and on a developer's laptop with yugabyted.

As the VP of Engineering for DBaaS, you will lead the teams that build, ship, and run every way customers consume YugabyteDB as a service. You will own the roadmap delivery, quality, and operation of YugabyteDB Aeon, Aeon BYOC, YugabyteDB Anywhere, and yugabyted. You will work across a modern cloud stack: Kubernetes on GKE, EKS, and AKS, Java frameworks, Python and shell automation, Terraform, and observability tooling across AWS, GCP, and Azure. You will be the executive owner of production for Aeon, setting the standard for incident response, on-call health, and the reliability our customers count on.

You will also own the Security and SRE charters for the DBaaS organization. That includes product and cloud security, vulnerability management, compliance programs such as SOC 2, and the SRE practices that keep Aeon highly available, performant, and cost-efficient around the clock. You will take responsibility for the resiliency, security, and cost of the architectural choices made across the organization, and stay close enough to the technology to lead design reviews and major incidents with your engineers.

You will lead a global organization of engineers, managers, and SREs across several geographies reporting to the SVP of Engineerin

The Vice President of Information Technology is responsible for developing and executing enterprise-wide technology strategies that advance business objectives, strengthen operational efficiency, enhance customer experience, and support long-term organizational growth and competitiveness. This role reports to the Chief Operating and Technology Officer (COTO), serving as a key member of the senior leadership team.

This position provides leadership and oversight across enterprise technology, infrastructure, business applications, data engineering, cybersecurity, and digital capabilities. The Vice President of Information Technology partners closely with executive leadership, internal business teams, technology professionals, and external stakeholders to modernize systems, optimize technology investments, strengthen security and resilience, and deliver scalable, reliable, and innovative technology solutions.

• Evaluate emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data analytics, and other digital capabilities, to identify opportunities for innovation and competitive advantage.

• Assess existing technology capabilities and recommend strategic investments, system enhancements, and technology solutions that improve business performance.

• Provide strategic direction for business applications, enterprise platforms, system architecture, and technology operations to ensure reliability, scalability, availability, and performance.

• Lead the implementation and integration of new technology platforms, including transition planning, deployment coordination, and change management.

• Oversee disaster recovery planning and technology resilience

Remote Position: Yes

Region: Americas

Summary

HPS (Hardware Platform Solutions), part of Celestica, designs and delivers data center hardware with leading hyper scale and technology customers. As Technical and Customer Facing Program Director, you are the single accountable technical owner of a strategic customer program, from concept through new product introduction (NPI) to volume ramp.

You report to VP of Operations Engineering act as the customer's primary technical contact, and lead a matrixed team of hardware, software, systems engineering, program management and new product development teams as one program team. You also work closely with supplier development, manufacturing and site NPI.

Detailed Description

Key responsibilities

•
Program delivery: own the integrated program plan (schedule, milestones, phase gates, budget, risks) and drive it through EVT/DVT/PPVT/PVT/Optimization, NPI and ramp to agreed quality, cost and time targets.

•
Phase-gate governance: ensures alignment at phase gate reviews with clear entry and exit criteria and make go/no-go recommendations.

•
Customer engagement: serve as the customer's primary technical contact; set and run the engagement cadence, from weekly technical syncs to quarterly business reviews.

•
Escalation: own the customer escalation path and resolve issues at the lowest effective level.

•
Cross-functional leadership: lead engineering and program teams through a matrix; set priorities and resolve trade-offs on design, resources and schedule.

•
Operating model: define and apply the program RACI, decision rights, change control and reporting.

•
Manufacturing readiness: bring design-for-manufacturability and design-for-test input in early, and confirm test readiness and process capability before each build.

•
Supply chain alignment: align supplier qualification, material readiness and line readiness with the program schedule.

•
Reporting: report program health to senior leadership and the customer, and close review actions on time.

Knowledge/Skills/Competencies

What success looks like

•
Phase gates and customer milestones met on plan.

•
Strong first-pass yield at each build, with manufacturability and test findings closed before NPI.

•
Program cost on budget.

•
High customer satisfaction and escalations resolved quickly.

What we look for

•
Ownership: you treat the product quality as your own.

•
Systems thinking: you see how hardware, software, test and manufacturing decisions affect each other.

•
Influence: you lead teams and partners through clarity and credibility, not reporting lines.

•
Customer credibility: you earn trust with senior customer stakeholders and raise problems early, with a plan.

•
Decisiveness and discipline: you make trade-off calls with incomplete information and run a tight operating cadence.

•
Global mindset: you work well across North American and Asian teams.

Physical Demands

Typical Experience

•
15+ years in hardware

Join the Controls Technology division as a Product Manager. In this strategic and high-impact role, you will own the vision, product strategy, and end-to-end lifecycle of mission-critical Risk and Control technology platforms across our global financial enterprise.

You will lead the transition from business problem spaces to scalable, compliant, and intuitive technical products. Working closely with senior business executives, risk officers, compliance partners, architecture leads, and dedicated Product Owners/Engineering teams, you will define the "Why" and "What" behind our product investments. This role is designed for a strategic product thinker and outcome-driven leader who balances visionary road mapping, rigorous risk governance, deep technical fluency, and modern AI-augmented delivery practices.

Key Responsibilities
1. Product Vision, Strategy & Road mapping
• Define & Own the Product Vision: Formulate and articulate a compelling multi-year product vision and roadmap for Controls Technology platforms aligned with global enterprise risk appetite, regulatory mandates, and business objectives.
• Drive Strategic Prioritization: Balance competing demands across regulatory commitments, business feature requests, technical debt remediation, and architecture modernization using data-driven prioritization frameworks (e.g., RICE, WSJF, Value vs. Complexity).
• Manage Product Lifecycle: Own the full product lifecycle from discovery and incubation through growth, optimization, and eventual decommissioning or legacy modernization.
2. Product Discovery & Business Value Realization
• Customer & Stakeholder Discovery: Lead continuous product discovery sessions with business leaders, compliance officers, operational risk managers, and auditors to uncover root problems and unmet operational needs.
• Define Key Metrics & Outcomes (OKRs/KPIs): Establish measurable business outcomes, adoption metrics, risk-reduction indices, and operational efficiency KPIs; monitor performance and iterate based on quantitative insights and qualitative user feedback.

This is a rare opportunity to join a team that is bringing an entirely new category of brain health to the world. At Cognito, we are developing therapies designed to promote dignity, clarity, and coherence in the lives they touch.

Cognito is a neurotechnology company developing a new therapeutic approach to cognitive and neurological health, designed to work with the brain's own activity and biology. Born from pioneering neuroscience research at MIT, Cognito brings together neuroscience, engineering, medicine and technology to translate breakthroughs in brain science into practical therapies designed for everyday life.

Our first therapeutic application, Spectris AD, is an investigational, prescription, at-home therapy for Alzheimer's disease. With our pivotal HOPE study now complete, Cognito is entering an important new phase as we advance Spectris AD toward regulatory review, prepare for potential commercialization and continue exploring the broader potential of our science across neurological health.

We are building an interdisciplinary team united by a shared purpose: protecting and progressing the human ability to think, learn and remember. For innovators who want to work at the intersection of breakthrough science, technology and human health, Cognito offers the chance to help shape what comes next.
About The Job

Cognito is building a Security, Privacy, and IT organization from the ground up under the SVP of Security, Privacy, and IT, structured across three functions. The Information Security Director leads the Information Security function day-to-day — hiring and running the team, and driving SOC 2 and HIPAA audit readiness to completion, with HITRUST in the future — under the strategic direction of the SVP, who holds overall executive (CISO-level) accountability for security.

Build & Lead the Information Security Function
• Stand up and run Information Security day-to-day: hire and manage a team.

Certification & Audit Readiness
• Drive SOC 2 and HIPAA audit preparation and execution end-to-end — scoping, control implementation, evidence collection, and auditor coordination.
• Build toward the multi-year HITRUST certification goal, reporting progress and risk up to the SVP.
Policy, Risk & Vendor Management
• Build and maintain the information security policy set (access control, data protection, vendor risk, incident response, etc) that the rest of the team will operate against.
• Establish a vendor security review process for new tools and vendors as the company scales.
Client & Partner Security Support
• Serve as the day-to-day technical security contact in partner and client diligence conversations, escalating to the SVP for executive-level or strategic discussions.
Interim Leadership & Team Growth
• Provide an interim reporting home for the Privacy Analyst, until the Privacy Director is hired.
• Hire and ramp the Security team.
