Overview

This is a hybrid role. 2 days remote (Monday, Friday) and 3 days onsite (Tuesday-Thursday)

The Director, Cloud Infrastructure is accountable for the strategy, reliability, and continuous improvement of the company's enterprise technology services, including infrastructure engineering, cloud platforms, and operational governance.

This role leads multiple technical and service delivery teams and serves as the primary owner of core IT operations that enable business continuity and teammate productivity across all locations. The Director balances long-term modernization initiatives with day-to-day operational excellence, ensuring systems are secure, resilient, scalable, and aligned with business growth.

The position partners closely with Security, Applications, Finance, and Audit to manage risk, maintain regulatory compliance, and deliver a stable and high-quality technology experience for the organization.
Who we are:

At Cube Smart, we're intentional about culture. You can experience it everywhere from our mission statement of "genuine care" to our "It's What's Inside That Counts" tagline to calling each other 'teammates' rather than employees. This spirit fosters a fun and collaborative environment that has resulted in our rapid growth and being recognized amongst the top in our industry.

Cube Smart's award-winning team is made up of people who genuinely care. Teammates care about our customers and the life events and/or business needs they are facing. Teammates are passionate, responsible and understanding. The Cube Smart team is made up of people who have a can-do attitude, are committed to their own success and the success of the company, and lead by example.

If this sounds like a team and culture that matches your personal values and motivations, we want to hear from you.

• Define and execute the multi-year roadmap for infrastructure and operations services
• Lead hybrid cloud strategy across Azure, AWS, and Microsoft 365
• Establish standards for availability, scalability, resiliency, automation, and cost optimization
• Drive lifecycle planning for compute, storage, networking, identity, and endpoint platforms
• Evaluate new technologies and vendors to modernize and simplify the environment
• Align infrastructure investments to business priorities and growth plans
Infrastructure & Platform Operations
• Own availability, performance, and security of:
• Data centers and hosted environments
• Cloud infrastructure (Azure, AWS, Microsoft 365)
• Core enterprise systems and identity services
• Backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity platforms
• Endpoint/device management platforms
• Ensure SLAs and operational targets are consistently achieved
• Lead incident, change, and problem management practices

• Provide senior-level technical escalation and decision-making

Job Description Summary

The Director, Infrastructure & Platform leads the team that creates standard, reliable environments on which Defense & Systems builds, tests, and delivers software. The team owns the secure platforms, shared services, and the single golden-path delivery pipeline that the organization's software developers depend on, so that delivery is dependable, on time, and to standard. The role runs the platform as a product, not as a help desk.

This is a people-leadership role accountable for both the operating model and the people who run it. The Director sets the platform roadmap and service standards, mandates the golden path that product teams adopt, and holds the team to FLIGHT DECK standard work and a bias toward flow. Success improves Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost by removing undifferentiated infrastructure work from every software team and replacing ad-hoc environments with a governed, consumable platform.
Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities Team leadership and talent
• Lead and develop the Infrastructure & Platform team — technical program management, platform and infrastructure engineering, and infrastructure architecture — with clear role clarity, objectives, and standard work for each seat
• Own the team’s performance and development; build a culture of ownership, flow, and continuous improvement
• Identify and remove obstacles on behalf of the team, and coach problem-solving at the point of work

Platform operating model and governance
• Own and mandate a single golden-path delivery pipeline — CI/CD, environments, and shared services — that all product teams adopt, and govern the exception process when a team cannot
• Operate the platform as a product: a named backlog, a published roadmap, and service standards for availability, support, change management, and SLAs
• Establish how platform change is requested, prioritized, approved, and released, and make that governance visible to the teams it affects
• Partner with Cyber Security to build security best practice into the platform by default, and scope the Dev Sec Ops capability gap as an explicit Phase 2 headcount ask

Delivery and reliability
• Ensure secure, reliable, and scalable infrastructure across cloud, on-premises, and edge environments in a defense context
• Set the operating rhythm — daily management, WOR, and MOR — that keeps reliability and delivery managed, not merely reported
• Partner with the four product-development software teams so the platform meets their current needs and anticipates their future ones

Cross-organization alignment
• Represent Infrastructure & Platform in the Tech Ops leadership cadence and align the platform roadmap to the enterprise and CDAIO baseline
• Partner with the Director, Architecture & Data so platform patterns and architecture guardrails stay coupled

Basic qualifications (required)
• Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or college with a minimum of 7 years of professional experience OR Associat

Chief Information Officer

Mission:

IDEA Public Schools is searching for a Chief Information Officer (CIO) who will report directly to the Deputy Superintendent of Operations and sit on the Executive Team. As an innovative and forward-thinking educational organization, we are seeking a visionary and inspirational CIO who will drive the strategic direction of the Information Systems & Technology (IST) area and lead its group of high-functioning team of technical and subject matter experts. The IST area creates value for end users—students, staff, and families—and empowers their decision-making with seamless integrations, process design, customized solutions, data insight generation, collaboration, and best-in-class customer service. The CIO will partner with cross-functional teams to ensure the effective integration of technology into our educational and operational ecosystem, the provision of reliable, secure, and robust infrastructure, and to build a truly data-driven culture of rigor and insight. A successful candidate will have an expansive mindset about a futuristic approach to technology and data, a people-first approach to innovation, value co-creation, and problem solving, and a proven track record of scaling complex information systems and solutions.

The CIO will manage the Vice Presidents of each division (Data Accountability and Compliance, Enterprise Applications, Information Technology, Technology Operations), the Director of Project Management Office, a Chief of Staff, and an Executive Assistant.

This is a full-time position based in Texas, with preference given to candidates who live in Austin, El Paso, Houston, Permian Basin (Midland/Odessa), Rio Grande Valley, San Antonio, and Tarrant County (Fort Worth), or who are willing to relocate.

Travel Expectations:

While this is a remote position, there will be in-person meetings across various regions. Candidates must be willing to travel up to 40% of the time during key implementation phases and go-live support periods.

The business is building a platform to help organizations understand how work is carried out, identify opportunities to improve and automate processes, and turn those insights into useful AI-enabled tools.

There is a working product and early customer interest. The CTO will take ownership of the technical direction, develop the product into an enterprise-ready platform and build the founding engineering team.

The opportunity

This is a true technical co-founder role. Working closely with the founding CEO and incubation team, you will:
• Define the technical architecture, product roadmap and engineering strategy.
• Build and develop the product from its current stage into a scalable enterprise platform.
• Remain hands-on during the early stages, particularly across the most important architectural and product decisions.
• Work directly with design partners to understand their workflows and translate real customer needs into technical solutions.
• Establish the approach to AI evaluation, security, privacy, reliability and enterprise deployment.
• Recruit and lead the early engineering team while creating a strong technical culture.

The technical challenge brings together applied AI, workflow intelligence, high-volume event data and automation. The platform will need to operate effectively within complex enterprise environments while handling sensitive workplace data in a secure and trusted way.

What we are looking for

We are looking for a deeply technical builder with the ambition and judgement to become a genuine co-founder.

The strongest candidates are likely to bring a combination of:
• Experience building AI-native products, agentic systems, developer tools, workflow platforms or enterprise automation products.
• Strong architecture and engineering fundamentals across scalable systems, data infrastructure and production AI.
• Experience with native or desktop applications, event-driven systems, on-device processing or other resource-constrained environments.
• A track record of taking products from an early prototype into reliable production use.
• The ability to work closely with customers and translate ambiguous business problems into focused technical decisions.
• Experience hiring and leading engineers while remaining close to the product and code.
• Genuine appetite for the ownership, pace and ambiguity of a zero-to-one company.

New York is strongly preferred, with an in-person approach expected during the formative stages of the business.

If you would be open to a confidential conversation, please contact Harry Sliufko at Kadence or send across your latest CV.

About Leadex Systems

Leadex Systems builds integration and API management platforms for banks, payment providers and government entities across the Middle East, Cyprus and Europe. We are 60 people. We have been a Mule Soft partner for years and were named Mule Soft Partner of the Year Middle East 2024 and Mule Soft Partner Champion Middle East 2025. Most of what we build lives in places where an integration failure is a regulatory event rather than a bad sprint: core banking, payments, onboarding, government service platforms.

Our clients run central bank audits, ISO 20022 migrations and multi-year complex implementations. We sit in the middle of complex digital transformations as an integration team connecting overall IT/IS landscape together.
What this role is

We are hiring a CTO to own the technical side of the company: how we design solutions, how we deliver them, and how our engineering organisation grows. You will report directly to founder (and current CTO) and CEO and sit on the leadership team. Day to day the job splits roughly three ways: architecture on our most complex programs, technical leadership of a distributed delivery team, and the engineering half of presales, where you shape the solution and defend it in front of a client's architecture board.

Our delivery portfolio today is mostly Mule Soft and Salesforce. We are not looking for a Mule Soft specialist. We are looking for an engineer who has spent a career on integration, has run genuinely hard programs, and can learn a platform in a quarter. If you have never touched Anypoint, we will get you through certification. What we cannot teach is the judgment that comes from having personally untangled a 200-interface landscape under a regulator's deadline.
• Solution architecture on flagship engagements. The bids that decide our year, and the delivery programs that follow them. You set the architecture, you review the critical decisions, and you are the person the client's chief architect argues with.
• Engineering standards across the practice. Integration patterns, API design, CI/CD and release strategy, non-functional requirements, how we estimate. Today these live in people's heads and in past project artefacts; we want them written down and enforced.
• Technical presales. Technical discovery, solution design, effort estimation, and the architecture sections of RFP responses. Our deals are won or lost on whether the client believes the design will survive their environment.
• The technical organisation. Hiring architects and senior engineers, growing the people already here, deciding what capability we build next and what we buy. We want a mentor, not a gatekeeper.

Convene Hospitality Group (CHG) operates a global portfolio of lifestyle brands focused on creating places and experiences that bring people together. The company designs, develops, and operates hospitality-driven destinations to host gatherings of all kinds, ranging from small corporate meetings to immersive brand activations and beyond. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well.

If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team.
Director, Cloud Infrastructure

We're hiring a Director of Cloud Infrastructure to join Convene Hospitality Group's (CHG) Technology organization. It's a hands-on role with an AI-native mindset. There are no direct reports today. You’ll lead through the platform, redesigning how we deploy and setting the standards our product and corporate engineering teams build on. You'll also run the cloud, AI, and venue infrastructure under our portfolio of brands, from client-facing experiences to the systems that keep our nearly 40 venues running.

This is a rebuild. You design it and you build it.

Today, deployments are manual and happen about once a sprint. That's the starting line. You'll rethink how we ship so that deployments are unlocked, safe, secure, and governed.

You'll have high autonomy and real decision-making power over the tools we use and how we build. We're committed to AWS and will build deeply on it. Most of what sits on top is fair game: CI tooling, pipeline design, orchestration patterns, and source control. A decision like Bitbucket versus Git Hub is a live call, and it's yours to make.

Legacy migration follows the decisions. You make the call, then you do the move. This role will have a lot of influence.

This is a wide seat. You’ll work across product and corporate engineering, and you’re a big part of how we get to AI-first, spec-driven development.
What You’ll Do:
• Rebuild the deployment path. Own CI/CD end to end: build, release, and rollback. Take us from manual deploys to an automated path.
• Make it safe, secure and governed. Access control, audit trails, secrets management, environment separation, and a rollback path any engineer can execute.
• Make the platform calls. Source control, CI tooling, orchestration, and infrastructure-as-code patterns. Jenkins is what we run today; what we run next is up to you. Decide, document the trade-off, then go forth and migrate.
• Run the AI gateway. Build and operate the layer between our engineers, agents and the models they call: provider routing, key management, rate limits, token metering, and usage logging. Every AI call should be visible, governed, and attributable.

Reports to: CTO

Department: Technology

Location: This is a fully remote U.S.-based position. Candidates must reside and work in one of the following states due to tax and compliance requirements: AR, AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, ID, IL, LA, MD, MO, NC, NJ, NV, NY, OH, TX, VA, WA, WI, or WY.

Tier 1 (Higher Cost Markets): $190,000 - $220,000

Tier 2 (National Markets): $180,000 - $210,000

Tier 3 (Lower Cost Markets): $170,000 - $200,000
About the Company

Paleovalley and Wild Pastures were born from a simple but radical idea: real food can heal — people, animals, and the planet. When Paleovalley co-founders Autumn and Chas Smith saw how industrialized food was affecting human health and the health of the land, they refused to play along. Autumn’s own journey of healing through nutrient-dense foods lit a fire that became Paleovalley. From there, the mission grew roots, sprouted wings, and eventually expanded into Wild Pastures to bring regeneratively raised meats directly to families nationwide.

Today, Paleovalley crafts deeply nourishing snacks and supplements made with organic ingredients and honorable sourcing. Wild Pastures connects small American farmers practicing regenerative agriculture with customers who believe better food is worth fighting for. Every product, every partnership, and every decision is guided by a commitment to real ingredients, regenerative practices, and the belief that health is built from the soil up.

We’re a team of grounded doers, curious thinkers, bold builders, and warm humans who like to laugh while doing meaningful work. We're growing quickly, fueled by purpose and a shared desire to repair the food system one thoughtful choice at a time. If you feel energized by impact, drawn to mission, and ready to join a company rewriting the future of food, we’d love to meet you!
About the Opportunity

The technology behind Paleovalley and Wild Pastures is central to how customers shop, subscribe, and get help - and how our teams fulfill orders and run the business. Much of it was built in-house by our co-founder and CTO. As both brands grow, we need a technology organization that can keep these platforms strong, connect them with our business systems, and support the next stage of growth.

The Vice President of Technology will be the CTO’s trusted right hand and lead the full technology function across software engineering, business systems, and IT. This leader will set priorities and investment plans with the CTO, make consequential day-to-day decisions with substantial autonomy, and own the team, budget, delivery, and health of our technology. Patrick Industries, a publicly traded company headquartered in Elkhart, Indiana, invites you to join a team of dedicated Team Members who are passionate about delivering high-quality products and exceptional customer service. As a leading solutions provider serving a diverse range of markets across the United States, our commitment to innovation, quality, and sustainability has positioned us as a high growth, diversified and empowered Team of more than 10,000! Your adventure awaits!

Patrick Industries is building its enterprise AI and data capability from the ground up — and is searching for the executive to lead it. This is a rare “zero-to-one” mandate inside a profitable, acquisitive company with 65+ years of entrepreneurial execution and 85+ operating brands: a staged, multi-year investment behind a use-case portfolio carrying more than $150M of identified value across 70+ initiatives, spanning customer-centric operations, aftermarket commerce, and back-office automation. The Vice President of AI & Data will set the operating model, formulate the AI and data investment strategy, build and scale the delivery team, own the data foundation on which it all depends, and run the engine that turns strategy into production-grade and measurable value.

The Role

Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Vice President of AI & Data governs, prioritizes, and delivers the enterprise AI, data, and automation initiatives that drive measurable business value across Patrick Industries. The role is the execution engine behind the enterprise AI strategy — and the steward of the data foundation beneath it — translating prioritized use cases into scalable, production-grade solutions through a DevOps-enabled, agile delivery model, and ensuring a disciplined delivery capability that is fast without being fragile.

Operating at the intersection of business and technology, the VP carries full lifecycle accountability — from intake and prioritization through build, deployment, and scaled adoption — and is expected to stay at the leading edge of a fast-moving field, continuously evaluating new models, agentic frameworks, and tools and translating them into pragmatic, well-governed advantage. The leader drives clear traceability from each use case to defined KPIs and business outcomes, strengthens the data-governance leg of the enterprise Digital Backbone, and aligns delivery to Patrick’s IT Strategic Pillars:
• Innovative Advantage – Scale AI-, data-, and automation-driven capabilities that unlock new business value.
• Value Optimization – Ensure measurable ROI, efficiency gains, and capital discipline.
• Agility & Efficiency – Enable rapid, iterative delivery through modern DevOps practices.
• Resilient Operations – Keep AI and data solutions secure, stable, and well-governed.

Areas of Responsibility

The mandate spans the operating capabilities the VP will stand up to govern, deliver, and sustain AI and data at enterprise scale.

• Partner with practice leaders to identify and execute revenue growth opportunities, including cross-selling, pricing optimization, and service expansion
• Evaluate and implement operational improvements that enhance scalability, profitability, and client experience

Why This Role:

This is a defining opportunity to lead one of the most technically ambitious and capital-intensive transformations in physical logistics — building the automation and AI systems that will define how goods move through a $10B enterprise's distribution network for the next decade. The successful candidate will have the mandate, budget, and executive alignment to deploy Physical AI and robotics at scale across a national DC footprint.

• Own the Physical AI and robotics strategy for one of the largest logistics companies in North America

• Significant scope: full technology ownership across DC, warehouse, yard, cross-dock, and emerging automation platforms

• High-visibility executive role with direct line to C-suite and meaningful influence over major capital investment decisions

• Rare chance to sit at the frontier of OT/IT convergence — deploying computer vision, autonomous systems, and real-time intelligence in live fulfillment operations

• Competitive total compensation including base, annual bonus, and long-term incentive plan

Position Summary:

The Vice President of Technology – Distribution & Warehouse serves as the senior technology executive responsible for designing, building, and operating the full suite of technology platforms that power the company's distribution, warehousing, and supply chain fulfillment operations. This executive owns the technology roadmap across Distribution Centers (DCs), Warehouse Management, Yard Management, Cross-Dock Operations, and emerging Physical AI applications — directly enabling the speed, accuracy, and throughput of the company's physical logistics network.

This role sits at the intersection of technology and physical operations — partnering with DC GMs, operations leadership, and supply chain executives to deploy systems that drive measurable improvements in order accuracy, labor productivity, inventory precision, and dock-to-dock cycle times. VP will be a key voice in enterprise architecture, automation investment decisions, and the company's Physical AI and robotics strategy as it scales across a national network of facilities.

This position is based in our Penske Logistics development center in Beachwood, OH. This is an in-office position, at least 4 days a week. Relocation assistance may be available for qualified candidates.

Major Responsibilities:

Technology Strategy & Roadmap

Ready to stop reporting to the CTO and become one?

This role puts you on the top technical seat for hardware that really matters.
What you'll get

This business builds advanced hardware systems for demanding customers and governments, and now needs a CTO to build its hardware.
• The top technical seat, not a seat under it
• Decisions that are still open. Suppliers, parts and firmware for production are being chosen now, so you'd set them rather than inherit them.
• Feedback from real-world use, not lab testing
What you'd actually do

You'd take the hardware into production with supply chain / manufacturing peers and get it built the same way every time. You'd also build the team that does it, working alongside a software engineering lead.

You won't be starting from a blank sheet. If you enjoy taking something that works and making it buildable at volume, this is for you.
Is this you?
• A former engineer with deep electrical experience, now leading
• You've taken hardware into production
• People have followed you from one company to another

This isn't a remote leadership role. Expect time on the floor and at suppliers, and 30-50% travel early on. If you'd rather lead from a laptop, it's not for you. If you want to be where the hardware is, it is.

United Way of Northern New Jersey (UWNNJ) is seeking a strategic, innovative, collaborative, and results-oriented Senior Vice President, Technology to lead its enterprise technology, data, cybersecurity, AI, digital innovation, and business transformation strategy.

Position Summary

The Vice President, Information Technology (VP, IT) is a senior leadership role accountable for the strategy, security, and day-to-day execution of Viventium's global corporate IT and information security functions. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, the VP, IT leads the design, delivery, and operation of technology and security solutions that support the organization's goals across its U.S., Costa Rica, United Kingdom, Canada, and India operations, and is responsible for ensuring the security, integrity, and availability of the company's data and IT infrastructure.

This role combines strategic planning with hands-on operational delivery. The VP, IT owns enterprise IT service delivery, cybersecurity operations, regulatory and audit compliance (e.g., SOC 1 / SOC 2), vendor and license management, and the technology integration of acquired businesses.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

The essential functions include, but are not limited to, the following:

• Develops and executes long- and short-term strategic and operational plans for corporate IT and security that align with company priorities, business needs, service and operational excellence, resource planning, and growth at scale.

• Manages and oversees the comprehensive enterprise information security (InfoSec) program to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the company's platforms, data, applications, networks, systems, servers, and endpoints in an operationally efficient and effective manner.

• Leads security operations, monitoring, and incident response in partnership with the company's managed SOC/EDR provider; performs risk analysis for existing and potential partners and providers.

• Owns regulatory and audit compliance, including SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type 2 evidence, the risk register, internal controls matrix, and coordination with external auditors and cyber-insurance carriers.

• Leads the technology and security integration of acquired businesses, including identity, email, SSO, security-baseline alignment, backup/DR readiness, and vendor consolidation.

• Establishes and enforces a Microsoft-first enterprise tooling strategy and AI governance framework (e.g., Microsoft 365, Purview, Copilot, Azure AI Foundry) with clear governance guardrails for approved AI tools.

• Oversees and governs Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery plan

About Charm
 
Our mission is to return the atmosphere to 280 ppm CO₂. We convert excess inedible biomass into carbon-rich bio-oil and inject it into underground storage for permanent carbon removal. At scale, we can use bio-oil to make fossil-free iron.
 
Our carbon removal efforts began in 2020 with initial purchases from customers like Stripe, Shopify, and Microsoft. Since then, we’ve scaled to thousands of tons of carbon removal, grown to over a hundred employees, and established three locations in San Francisco, Colorado, and Louisiana.
 
We're expanding our team of ambitious, creative, and hands-on problem solvers. We value psychological safety, collaboration, and continuous learning. We take calculated risks and treat mistakes as opportunities to improve. If you're excited about tackling big challenges, we encourage you to explore our company values.
 
Come help us reverse climate change. Gigatons or bust!

Reporting to the CTO, you will work directly and often with Charm's executive team, bringing program status, risks, and tradeoff recommendations to the decisions that shape the company. Rezo is a different kind of biopharma company. Our mission is to dramatically increase the success rate of drug development by building a disease-agnostic, fully-integrated, network biology platform that will redefine our understanding of human disease and ability to treat it.

- Influences peer leaders and senior stakeholders across the business, product, and technology teams

- Formal training or certification on software engineering concepts and 10+ years applied experience. In addition, 5+ years of experience leading technologists to manage, anticipate and solve complex technical items within your domain of expertise
- Experience developing or leading cross-functional teams of technologists
- Experience with hiring, developing, and recognizing talent

onsemi is hiring a Senior Director to lead its PMIC (Power Management IC) and POL (Point-of-Load) product development. You will set the technical direction and run day-to-day execution for a global team of analog, mixed-signal, digital and layout engineers spread across four sites.

You will own each product from start to finish: defining it with Marketing and Systems, then leading architecture, design, verification, tape-out, silicon validation, qualification and release to production. You will be accountable for schedule, quality, cost and first-pass silicon success. The role combines deep technical knowledge of power management with strong organizational leadership and close work with customers.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy and Product Leadership
- Set and carry out the technical roadmap for PMIC and POL products (multi-rail PMICs, buck, boost, buck-boost, LDOs, and digitally controlled/PMBus POL converters) for data center/AI compute, and consumer markets.
- Work with Marketing, Business Units and Systems/Applications to turn customer and market needs into competitive product definitions and specifications.
- Track the competition and new technologies, and find chances to stand out on efficiency, power density, transient response, integration and cost.
- Work with Process Technology to make the best use of onsemi BCD and other process platforms for power management products.

End-to-End Product Development
- Own the full development cycle: concept, architecture, design, layout, verification, tape-out, silicon bring-up, characterization, qualification and release to manufacturing.
- Make sure projects meet schedule, cost, performance and quality targets, with a strong focus on first-pass silicon success.
- Set up and enforce design methodology, design reviews, verification rigor (including mixed-signal/AMS) and documentation standards.
- Work with Product Engineering, Test, Applications, Packaging, Quality and Operations to make sure products are manufacturable and can be ramped smoothly.

Organizational Leadership
- Lead, grow and develop a global, multi-site organization of managers and engineers in Hudson, Rhode Island, San Jose and Bangalore.
- Build a team that performs well, works together and is inclusive, with clear accountability and consistent practices across sites.
- Hire, keep and mentor top technical talent.
- Plan resources, budgets and headcount across several programs running at the same time.

In this role you would lead the software development organization building out and operating these systems and work with some of the largest players in the AI space building systems that operate at unprecedented speed, scale and reliability. - Working with geographically distributed teams and contribute to the success of their and of other related teams.

- MS or BS in Computer Science, or equivalent experience
- 5+ years of experience managing Software Engineering teams.
- 12+ years of software engineering experience
- Strong communication skills, analytical skills, and project management skills

Discover Your Future in Credit Risk Technology
Build systems that shape credit decisions—at scale.
Join a fast-moving Credit Risk Technology team where modern engineering, data, and AI come together to drive real-world financial impact. We operate with a startup mindset—ownership, speed, and experimentation—within the rigor and responsibility of a global financial institution. You’ll help design and deliver mission-critical platforms that support credit risk assessment, analytics, and decisioning across the firm.

Job Overview

The Credit Risk Applications Technology Lead Analyst is a senior engineering leadership role focused on building and evolving modern, scalable platforms for credit risk management. You will lead application design and development while partnering closely with risk, data, and platform teams to deliver systems that are performant, resilient, and compliant.

This role blends hands-on development, system architecture, technical leadership, and AI-enabled innovation, with a strong emphasis on microservices, cloud-native design, and enterprise-grade governance.

Key Responsibilities
- Architect, design, and deliver scalable, Python-based applications supporting credit risk analytics, workflows, and reporting.
- Partner with risk, product, and technology leadership to integrate platforms, identify enhancements, and enable new products and process improvements.
- Resolve high-impact, complex initiatives through deep analysis of business processes, system flows, and industry standards.
- Ensure solutions adhere to enterprise architecture, data, security, and infrastructure blueprints.
- Establish and enforce engineering standards for coding, testing, CI/CD, debugging, and production readiness.
- Design and evolve microservices-based architectures, ensuring scalability, resiliency, observability, and maintainability.
- Apply AI and GenAI capabilities to modernize workflows, automate analysis, and unlock new insights in credit risk.
- Serve as technical leader and mentor, coaching mid-level engineers and analysts and allocating work as needed.
- Apply sound risk and control judgment, ensuring compliance with laws, regulations, and policies while safeguarding clients, data, and the firm.

How You’ll Work
- Operate with a startup mindset: ownership, bias for action, and pragmatic innovation.
- Deliver with enterprise discipline: stability, controls, transparency, and audit readiness.
- Balance experimentation with responsibility in a high-trust, high-impact environment.
- Adapt quickly as priorities change while maintaining long-term system integrity.

Core Technical Skills
- 10–15 years of experience in application development or systems engineering within complex environments.
- Advanced proficiency in Python and SQL , with strong software engineering fundamentals.
- Hands-on experience building API-driven services using FastAPI, Pydantic, and/or Django.

Citi, the leading global bank, has approximately 200 million customer accounts and does business in more than 160 countries and jurisdictions. Citi provides consumers, corporations, governments, and institutions with a broad range of financial products and services, including consumer banking and credit, corporate and investment banking, securities brokerage, transaction services, and wealth management.

As a bank with a brain and a soul, Citi creates economic value that is systemically responsible and, in our clients’, best interests. As a financial institution that touches every region of the world and every sector that shapes your daily life, our Enterprise Operations & Technology teams are charged with a mission that rivals any large tech company. Our technology solutions are the foundations of everything we do from keeping the bank safe, managing global resources, and providing the technical tools our workers need to be successful to designing our digital architecture and ensuring our platforms provide a first-class customer experience. We reimagine client and partner experiences to deliver excellence through secure, reliable, and efficient services.

Our commitment to diversity includes a workforce that represents the clients we serve from all walks of life, backgrounds, and origins. We foster an environment where the best people want to work. We value and demand respect for others, promote individuals based on merit, and ensure opportunities for personal development are widely available to all. Ideal candidates are innovators with well-rounded backgrounds who bring their authentic selves to work and complement our culture of delivering results with pride. As a Lead Front End Software Engineer, you will drive the design and delivery of modern web applications using JavaScript and Angular within Citi's Technology organization. You will own the technical direction of front end systems, partner with teams across the business to shape new product capabilities, and mentor developers as you deliver solutions at scale. - Subject matter expertise in at least one area of applications development.
- Demonstrated leadership and project management capabilities, including the ability to reprioritize work quickly as business needs change.
- Clear and concise written and verbal communication skills.
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Beneficial Skills & Qualifications
- Master's degree in a related field.

What We Offer

Based in Citi's Jersey City technology location, this role gives you the platform to grow your technical expertise while shaping how front end engineering is delivered across a global organization.
- A hybrid work model, with 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely.
- Opportunities to lead technical projects within a global technology organization.
- Access to continuous learning and professional development resources.
- Benefits supporting financial wellbeing and work-life balance.
- A collaborative, performance-driven team environment.
Apply now to lead front end engineering delivery at Citi.

The Applications Development Technical Lead Analyst is a senior engineering and architectural leadership role based in India, operating as a key regional anchor within the global Position Management technology organization.

The Vice President (VP) / Senior Software Engineer – Technical Remediation & Enablement Lead is a hands-on, code-level technical specialist responsible for driving the direct remediation of software vulnerabilities across enterprise application teams. This individual contributor / team-level technical lead works alongside application developers and contractor engineers to fix static code vulnerabilities (SAST), patch vulnerable software dependencies (SCA/third-party libraries), containerize workloads, and streamline local build/release pipelines to achieve same-day vulnerability hotfix and deployment capabilities .
This role combines active software engineering (writing/refactoring code and debugging pipelines) with technical enablement, guiding squad developers on how to adopt internal security and build tools, resolve tricky dependency conflicts, and package applications into modern containers for rapid, low-risk production releases.

Key Responsibilities & Core Duties
1. Hands-On Code Remediation & Dependency Patching
- Write, refactor, and review application code to directly remediate static code analysis (SAST) findings (e.g., SQL/command injection, cross-site scripting, insecure deserialization, improper error handling, weak cryptography).
- Resolve complex third-party library and framework upgrades (SCA/CVE remediation), managing transitive dependency conflicts, breaking API changes, and version incompatibilities across Java, Python, Go, .NET, or JavaScript/TypeScript stacks.
- Implement targeted automated unit, integration, and regression tests to validate that code fixes and patched libraries do not introduce functional regressions.
2. Containerization & Same-Day Release Enablement
- Work directly in application repositories to write and optimize Dockerfile s, container manifests, and base image configurations (Docker, OCI, Kubernetes/OpenShift).
- Assist application squads in containerizing non-containerized legacy services, establishing minimal base images and automated base-image rebuild triggers for same-day OS/runtime patching.
- Help configure and fine-tune CI/CD build scripts and release pipelines to compress deployment cycle times and eliminate manual deployment steps for emergency hotfixes.
3. Application Plan Technical Validation
- Perform code-level reviews of proposed remediation plans from application teams, verifying whether proposed library version bumps or refactored logic effectively eliminate the root cause of the vulnerability.
- Identify technical prerequisites (e.g., test coverage gaps, build tool upgrades, compiler/runtime updates) needed before a team can successfully patch and release.
4. Contractor Squad Pairing & PR Review
- Act as a peer reviewer and technical guide for external contractor engineers assigned to assist with remediation work.
- Review contractor-submitted pull requests (PRs) for code cleanliness, security correctness, test coverage, and enterprise architectural standards.

The Program Director, Water / Wastewater provides senior leadership and oversight for the successful delivery of large, complex water/wastewater programs of significant strategic and public value across the United States.
The role has been established to strengthen leadership readiness for critical water and wastewater pursuits and to support long-term succession planning for our active programs, ensuring experienced program leadership is in place to transition seamlessly from pursuit through delivery.

Current Programs include municipal drinking water systems, wastewater treatment facilities, collection and conveyance networks, water reuse, regulatory compliance and consent decree programs, climate resilience initiatives as well as major capacity expansion and rehabilitation efforts.

The Program Director sets the overall direction for program delivery, establishing governance, technical assurance, commercial frameworks, and integrated management systems required to meet client objectives, regulatory obligations, and community expectations.
Acting as the primary leader for day-to-day integration and performance, the role oversees multidisciplinary teams across engineering, construction management, environmental compliance, commercial management, and stakeholder engagement.

In addition to delivery leadership, the role plays a key part in work winning, contributing to capture strategy, proposal development, and client engagement for high-priority pursuits.
Due to the nature of this role, the initial work location may be flexible.  However, relocation to a program location will be required once a suitable program has been identified and awarded.  Current program locations include Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Atlanta and Dallas.
Key Responsibilities
- Provide senior leadership across the full lifecycle of major water/wastewater programs, from pursuits and mobilization

MAKE YOUR MARK. SECURE THE AI REVOLUTION.
About Axiado
Axiado builds hardware-rooted, AI-driven security and management silicon to make data centers more secure, efficient, and reliable. Its Trusted Control/Compute Unit (TCU) anchors an Intelligent Hardware Management Fabric that monitors and protects every component in the rack from below the OS.

Position Overview
At Axiado , we are redefining security, platform management, and energy efficiency for AI and cloud data centers. As Director of Product Management , you will own the multi-year roadmap and commercial strategy for our Trusted Control/Compute Unit (TCU) SoCs, Platform Intelligence Controllers (PIC) , and DC-SCM modules—driving flagship products from initial definition to silicon bring-up.
You will lead a lean team of Technical Product Managers while personally authoring core specs, building TCO models, and leading technical architecture deep-dives with hyperscalers and Tier-1 OEMs/ODMs.
Key Responsibilities
- Product Definition: Author flagship PRDs and MRDs, translating customer workloads into granular hardware, firmware, and on-chip AI specifications.
- Portfolio & TCO Strategy: Own the multi-generational TCU/PIC roadmap, pricing, and P&L. Build bottom-up TCO and power-savings models proving rack-level ROI.
- Team Leadership: Mentor and scale a lean team of PMs, setting the bar for technical rigor through active spec reviews and direct execution.
- Hyperscaler & Ecosystem Design-Wins: Lead technical and commercial engagements with CSPs, Tier-1 OEMs/ODMs, and silicon partners (Arm, NVIDIA, x86) to secure design-wins and shape OCP standards.
- Cross-Functional Co-Design: Partner daily with Silicon, Firmware, and AI Engineering on Performance-Power-Area (PPA), Dynamic Voltage & Frequency Scaling (DVFS), Hardware Root of Trust (RoT), and out-of-band telemetry.
- End-to-End Execution: Drive silicon from concept through tape-out, post-silicon bring-up, customer sampling, and production ramp alongside FAE, Marketing, and Operations.

Required Qualifications
- Education: BS in EE, CE, CS, or related technical field; MS, PhD, or MBA preferred.
- Experience: 10–12+ years in semiconductor product management, silicon architecture, or systems engineering, including 3+ years leading and mentoring PMs .
- Proven Silicon Track Record: Driven at least two complex SoCs or ASICs from initial PRD through tape-out and volume production.
- Domain Mastery: 5+ years of deep expertise in data center hardware—specifically BMCs, Hardware Root of Trust (RoT), DC-SCM modules, SmartNICs/DPUs, or network switches .
- Technical Fluency: Comfortable whiteboarding with principal architects; strong command of server management, out-of-band telemetry, OCP specs, and low-level interfaces ( PCIe, eSPI, MCTP, LTPI ).
- Commercial & Executive Agility: Proven ability to win hyperscale and Tier-1 designs while pivoting effortlessly from datasheet reviews to executive pitches.
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with AI-dri

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.
Why join the Harvard Radcliffe Institute?
The Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University, known colloquially as Harvard Radcliffe Institute, is one of the world’s leading centers for interdisciplinary exploration. We bring together students, scholars, artists, and practitioners to pursue curiosity-driven research, expand human understanding, and grapple with questions that demand insight from across disciplines.
The Fellowship Program annually supports the work of 50 leading artists and scholars. Academic Ventures fosters collaborative research projects and sponsors lectures and conferences that engage scholars with the public. The Schlesinger Library documents the lives of American women of the past and present for the future, furthering the Institute's commitment to women, gender, and society. The Emerging Leaders Program is a youth leadership development program partnering local high school sophomores with Harvard undergraduates in a mentoring relationship.
The Institute’s work is shaped by its history as the former Radcliffe College—a school founded to ensure that the standard of education embodied in Harvard was accessible to women, who were then excluded from the University. But the legacy of Radcliffe College is not simply coeducation at Harvard; it is the recognition that universities will always be greater when they draw wisdom and talent from the widest possible pool.
Take a look at this video to get different staff perspectives on working at Harvard Radcliffe Institute !

Oxfam is a global organization that fights inequality to end poverty and injustice. We offer lifesaving support in times of crisis and advocate for economic justice, gender equality, and climate action. We demand equal rights and equal treatment so that everyone can thrive, not just survive.

Location: Remote, anchored to either our Boston, MA, or Washington, DC, office. The Vice President works remotely day-to-day but is expected to maintain a regular, established presence at one of these offices and to come in as needed, with the specific rhythm set in coordination with the CEO.
Candidates must reside within commuting distance of Boston or DC. Candidates based in the New York area who can readily travel to either office by train are also encouraged to apply.
Employment type: Full-time, exempt
Department: Executive Office
Compensation: USD 235,000 to USD 250,000 per year
Reports to: President and CEO; dotted-line relationship to the Executive Vice President – Sr. Advisor to the President and CEO
Direct reports: CFO, Senior Director, Technology & Information Management (TIM), Head of People, Culture and Human Resources (PCHR)
Key collaborations: Oxfam America’s Senior Leadership Team; leaders across Finance, TIM, PCHR, and other operational functions; Oxfam International and affiliate teams; the Board and relevant Board committees; and external advisors, auditors, vendors, and consultants.
Job Description
Purpose of the position
The Vice President, Operations and Risk Management (VP O&RM) provides strategic and operational leadership for Oxfam America’s Operations and Risk Management division, including Finance, Technology and Information Management (TIM), and People, Culture and Human Resources (PCHR). As a member of the executive leadership team, the VP ensures that Oxfam America’s operational systems, infrastructure, people processes, financial stewardship (including grants management), risk management, compliance, and shared services are integrated, effective, agile, and aligned with organizational priorities and values. The VP leads and integrates the division’s functions and senior leaders as a single high-performing team for harmonized operational support, with a clear understanding of how interconnected and interdependent these functions are.
The VP represents Oxfam America with operational leaders across the Oxfam confederation to support and influence the ongoing priority of harmonizing and streamlining shared systems. The VP builds alignment and advances improvement and accountability through influence, negotiation, strong relationships, diplomacy, and sound judgment.
Why this role
You will lead a team of experienced senior functional leaders, each with deep specialist expertise, and report directly to the President and CEO. At Xplor, we believe that helping people make the most of each day is the most rewarding way to spend ours.
We give small and medium-sized businesses cloud-based, intuitive technology solutions that enable them to manage all the hassles of running and growing a business, so business owners can get back to doing what they love. With Xplor Pay, we help businesses get paid quickly and securely – without hidden fees. We built the tech ourselves, and our platform delivers secure, transparent, fast, and accurate payments.
We are unified by our purpose of helping people to succeed. So, when you become part of our team, you also become part of the personal connection that strengthens the relationship people have with Xplor products.

Position overview
The Head of AI/ML R&D decides, with evidence, whether an AI system works, how well, for whom, and at what cost. They come from data science and machine learning, and they build today with AI-native tools and agentic development.
The role owns the science of evaluation across every agent, the predictive and decision models behind the shared agents (churn, demand, payment recovery, fraud), and the experiment design that lets Finance count AI value once, against a holdout.
The role is hands-on. At least 50% of time goes to building models, evals and experiments; the rest to setting methods, reviewing, and growing a small team. This role makes what engineers ship measurable, cheaper and trustworthy, and supplies the models where an LLM alone is the wrong tool.
Key responsibilities
1. Evaluation science for every agent
o Set the enterprise eval methodology: golden-set design, sampling, labelling and inter-rater agreement, LLM-as-judge validation, slice analysis and statistical thresholds.
o Own the quality signals in the minimum telemetry contract: task success, groundedness, hallucination and escalation rates.
o Re-run evals per BU and tenant on every agent-core upgrade; catch regressions before customers do.
2. Predictive and decision models behind the shared agents
o Build and run the models the horizontal pods need: churn and retention uplift, payment-recovery propensity and timing, demand and capacity forecasting, later fraud and onboarding risk.
o Choose the right tool per task: classical ML, a small or fine-tuned model, retrieval, or a frontier LLM.
o Ship models to production on the golden path, with monitoring for drift and feedback loops.
3. Model economics
o Build the evidence behind model routing: accuracy, cost and latency per task, so routing is a measured decision.
o Drive cost per successful task down through distillation, caching strategy, smaller models and prompt and context optimization.
4. AI-native R&D and horizon scanning
o Prototype varied techniques (agent memory, planning, multi-agent patterns, synthetic data) against real Xplor problems.
o Turn what works into reference implementations in the golden path; retire what doesn't.
o Bring a monthly view of what has changed in models and met

Each day, you will manage cybersecurity risks that could affect the ABB brand and customer base for all ABB offerings, in a cost-effective way. - M.Sc. or higher degree in Software Development, Engineering or a related field.
- 15+ years of progressive cybersecurity experience in R&D or a related field.
- Proven experience working in a complex, global organization with accountability in the cybersecurity domain.

- Advanced knowledge of cybersecurity regulations and compliance requirements.

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description
The Director, Third-Party Cyber Defense is Allstate’s senior leader for supplier cyber incident response. The role is accountable for how quickly and appropriately Allstate understands and responds when a supplier is compromised. This leader sets direction for two functions: Supplier Incident Investigation & Response, and Supplier Monitoring & Intelligence. The Director also owns the technical inventory of supplier connections and leads targeted technical assessments when incidents, intelligence, or monitoring signals call for a closer look.

The role calls for an experienced incident response leader who understands how suppliers connect to large enterprises and can build a team that performs consistently under pressure. As a member of the Cyber Defense & Response leadership team, the Director partners with Enterprise TPRM, Procurement, Legal & Privacy, and Security Operations. Together they deliver fast, fact-based answers about Allstate’s exposure and a stronger supplier ecosystem after every event.

As a Director, you won’t just deliver results – you drive our culture and shared purpose. You can work remotely and will commute to a nearby office and/or travel for meaningful connection opportunities.

A supplier just told us they’ve been breached.
It is now one of the most common ways a cyber incident reaches a large company: a claims vendor, a payroll provider, a SaaS platform, a file-transfer service. The notice is usually short and vague. From that moment, five questions decide whether Allstate handles it well:
- Do they have our data? Which data, about which customers, in which states.
- How do they reach us? Every network link, API, file transfer, and service account, and whether we can shut each one down safely.
- What did we already know about them? Their risk tier, their last assessment, and the findings that are still open.
- What do they owe us? The notification, cooperation, and audit terms in their contract, and whether they are living up to them.
- What is the right response? Action that fits the facts: enough to protect our customers, without shutting down a business process when the facts don’t call for it.

The best third-party programs answer all five within hours, every time. Not because someone heroic stays up all night, but because the assessments were done, the connections were mapped, the playbook was practiced, and the working relationships with Legal, Privacy, Procurement, and Security Operations were in place before the call came.

About this role

The Aladdin Platform Engineering – Engineering Services team builds the platforms, pipelines, and developer tooling that thousands of engineers across BlackRock use every day to design, build, and ship software. Security is engineered into that path rather than inspected at the end of it: the same teams that own build systems, artifact repositories, and deployment pipelines also own the guardrails, evidence, and automated controls that make secure delivery the default.

You will lead the cybersecurity engineering function inside this group, working alongside platform engineering, product management, risk, and the firm’s information security organization to protect a large, cloud-native, AI-enabled, highly regulated financial services firm.

As Director for Cybersecurity Engineering, you’ll set the technical strategy for how security is built into software delivery and cloud infrastructure at scale. Software supply chain integrity is your first principle: every artifact the firm ships should carry verifiable provenance, and every release should be attested — signed, traceable to its source and build environment, and admissible as evidence without anyone assembling it after the fact. You’ll lead BlackRock toward that future state, moving the organization from periodic inspection of what was built to continuous, cryptographic proof of how it was built, with trust decisions made against attestations rather than assumptions.

You’ll treat DevSecOps as the operating principle that makes this achievable — policy as code, automated enforcement in continuous integration and delivery pipelines, and time-boxed exceptions with audit-ready evidence generated automatically. Staff Full-Stack Engineer (Director IC)

As a Staff Engineer at Capital One, you will be part of a community of technical experts working to define the future of banking in the cloud. You will work alongside our talented team of developers, machine learning experts, product managers and people leaders. Our Staff Engineers are leading experts in their domains, helping devise practical and reusable solutions to complex problems. You will drive innovation at multiple levels, helping optimize business outcomes while delivering strong technology solutions.

At Capital One, we believe diversity of thought strengthens our ability to influence, collaborate and provide the most innovative solutions across organizational boundaries. You will promote a culture of engineering excellence and strike the right balance between lending expertise and providing an inclusive environment where the ideas of others can be heard and championed. You will lead the way in creating next-generation talent for Capital One Tech, mentoring engineers and actively recruiting to keep building our community.

Staff Engineers are expected to lead through technical contribution. You will operate as a trusted advisor for our key technologies, platforms and capability domains, creating clear and concise communications, code samples, blog posts and other materials to share knowledge both inside and outside the organization. You will specialize in a particular subject area, but your input and impact will be sought and expected throughout the organization.

The Global Payment Network (GPN) Technology organization designs, builds, and operates the mission-critical systems and infrastructure that seamlessly power complex money movement across domestic and international rails. Sr. Director, Tech Risk & Analysis

Do you love navigating complex technology landscapes and safeguarding critical systems? Do you enjoy solving complex business problems in a fast-paced, collaborative, inclusive, and risk-conscious delivery environment? At Capital One, you'll be part of a big group of makers, breakers, doers and disruptors who love to solve real problems and meet real customer needs. We are seeking Tech Risk & Analysis Professionals who are passionate about cyber best practices, threat analysis, and risk mitigation to join our team. Job Description Summary:

Data is increasingly central to how the North America Operating Unit (NAOU) and its bottling partners understand the market, serve customers, improve execution, and make commercial decisions. Realizing that value often requires more than technology, it requires a leader who can connect business priorities, data capabilities, operating processes, and decision-makers across a complex system.
The Director, Data Enablement & Standards will lead high-priority efforts that make data easier to understand, access, connect, and use across NAOU and the North America system. This leader will work across business teams, Bottlers, Data & AI, and enabling functions to identify barriers, shape practical solutions, establish clear ways of working, and move cross-functional priorities from ambiguity to sustained action.
Initial areas of focus are expected to include strengthening how NAOU manages and realizes value from third-party data and advancing shared data standards across the North America system. Over time, the role may take on additional data enablement priorities where stronger coordination, common approaches, and focused leadership can help the system move faster and make better decisions.

Role purpose
Lead strategic data enablement priorities that require coordination across business, technical, and system partners, translating business needs into shared standards, repeatable processes, and clear accountability. The role owns the approach, coordination, and progress on agreed priorities, while business, specialist, and technical teams retain ownership of their data, decisions, and platforms.
Key responsibilities
- Shape the data enablement portfolio. Identify and prioritize opportunities where common approaches, stronger coordination, or focused leadership can unlock business value from data. Establish clear outcomes, roadmaps, decision rights, and measures of progress.
- Turn complex needs into practical action. Translate business challenges into achievable data, process, standards, governance, and operating-model improvements. Develop options, clarify tradeoffs, recommend a path, and move stakeholders toward decisions.
- Build alignment across the North America system. Bring together NAOU, Bottlers, CONA, CCBSS, and enabling functions around shared priorities. Build commitment through business value and practical recommendations.
- Improve how data moves from need to use. Examine the processes through which data is identified, acquired, defined, maintained, accessed, shared, and applied. Resolve unclear handoffs, fragmented ownership, duplication, and other barriers that slow progress.
- Advance shared data standards. Lead priority efforts to align definitions, hierarchies, attributes, mappings, and related ways of working where greater consistency creates meaningful business or technical value.
- Increase the value of external data. Lead and operate how NAOU identifies, acquires, governs, shares, and uses third-party data

Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team.

Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder.

Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, and France.

As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process.

We understand there may be occasional circumstances requiring accommodation and are happy to discuss them as needed. Your recruiter will be able to clarify expectations and answer any questions you have.

コレクターズ（Collectors）は、世界中のコレクターの皆様に付加価値の高いサービスを提供する、革新的なテクノロジーのリーディングカンパニーです。私たちは、数百万点に及ぶ記録的な価値を持つコレクターズアイテムのグレーディング、真贋鑑定、保管、および販売を行っています。また、コレクターの皆様が自身の情熱を追求できるよう支援するというというミッションのもと、これらのプロセスの近代化とデジタル化にも注力しています。現在、成長を続ける私たちのチームに加わっていただける人材を常に募集しています。

当社のサービス対象は、トレーディングカード、サイン、コミック、コイン、ビデオゲーム、イベントチケット、メモラビリアなど多岐にわたります。主な傘下ブランドには、PSA、PCGS、Beckett、SGC、Card Ladderが含まれます。

当社の面接プロセスの一環として、ビデオ面接の際はカメラをオンにしていただくようお願いしております。これにより、より充実した対話を促し、実際の職場環境に近い環境を再現するためです。なお、選考の段階によっては電話で実施する場合もございます。また、リモートワークの職種においても、弊社の判断により、選考の最終段階としてオンサイトでの面接をお願いする場合がございます。

The Lab is a vibrant unit within Cornell's College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS), where twelve world-class, mission-driven programs are directed by full-time faculty and other renowned professionals. workday:crowdstrike:R30677.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

About The Role:
We are looking for a Senior Director to build and lead the organization that turns the Lab’s research into AI security systems running in the real world. You will lead teams of engineers and research scientists who take frontier models and autonomous agents from promising results to production capabilities, on the Falcon sensor, where every millisecond, megabyte and CPU cycle counts, and across the cloud, where systems reason over trillions of events every day.
This role combines people leadership, technical depth and strategic influence. You will set the engineering strategy and roadmap, hire and develop exceptional leaders, and own delivery of systems that customers depend on. You will also stay close enough to the technology to challenge an architecture, debate a model choice with researchers and explain the tradeoffs clearly to executives. You will build for what is possible today while preparing the organization for what the next 12 to 24 months of model and agent capability will make possible.
If you have built and led the teams that shipped AI to stop adversaries in production, on the endpoint or at cloud scale, and you want to define what autonomous cyber defense looks like next, we want to talk.

About The Lab:
AI is changing cyber offense and defense at the same time. Adversaries now use models to inspect code, hunt for vulnerabilities, adapt tooling and run longer operations, and the fastest eCrime breakouts are measured in seconds. CrowdStrike built the Cybersecurity Superintelligence Lab to make sure defenders stay ahead.
The Lab is CrowdStrike’s frontier AI research organization for cyber defense. We advance the science and engineering of AI for security,

Director of Architecture, Advisory Technology

Job Description Summary
Cushman & Wakefield is hiring a Director of Advisory Architecture to lead architecture for its advisory business, improve the tools and processes that speed up development, and champion forward deployed engineering (FDE). The Director is an architect first, and the role has three parts: sound architecture for advisory solutions, ongoing optimization of development tools and processes (including accelerators such as AI Studio), and championing the FDE model of embedded, prototype-first delivery.

Job Description
Cushman & Wakefield is hiring a Director of Advisory Architecture to lead architecture for its advisory business, improve the tools and processes that speed up development, and champion forward deployed engineering (FDE). The Director is an architect first, and the role has three parts: sound architecture for advisory solutions, ongoing optimization of development tools and processes (including accelerators such as AI Studio), and championing the FDE model of embedded, prototype-first delivery.
The role combines deep solution and cloud architecture, including platforms such as Salesforce, with hands-on experience in agentic architecting and rapid, embedded development. The goal is for fast prototypes and AI-assisted work to be promoted into production by Engineering without rework, and for the architecture behind them to hold up.
The Director reports to the Head of Architecture and partners closely with Product, Business Analysis, Solution Architecture, and Engineering. Our customers are internal: brokers, other employees, and contractors who need technology that fits how they work.

What you will do
- Own architecture for the advisory business. Set the target architecture, standards, and roadmap for advisory solutions, and make sure designs are sound, secure, and consistent with company architecture standards.
- Optimize tools and processes. Continuously improve the tools, templates, and ways of working that shorten the development lifecycle from idea to production, including accelerators such as AI Studio.
- Practice agentic architecting. Define how AI agents are used to draft requirements, design solutions, and generate code, with human review, clear patterns, and quality controls at each step.
- Champion FDE. Lead and grow an embedded team that works with brokers and delivery teams to build working solutions quickly, iterate live on feedback, and decide with the business sponsor whether each effort is productized, handed off, or retired.
- Protect the path to production. Work with peer architecture leaders and Engineering on the guardrails prototypes are built within, a promotion gate to production, and shared source control, environments, and standards.
- Triage with Product. Agree on criteria for which requests enter the FDE lane and which follow the standard requirements, design, and build path, and cap FDE capacity so it does not become a help desk.

As a senior engineering leader at Generac, you will lead a team of systems engineers who own the end-to-end architecture, integration, and validation of industrial diesel and gaseous-fueled generator sets. Job Overview

The Institute for Technology Law and Policy is a prominent academic and research program in technology law and policy, comprising twenty faculty, staff, and students. The Institute houses interdisciplinary research projects of significant reach and impact. It is funded by public and private funders including government funding agencies, nonprofit foundations, and private donors. It coordinates a Tech Law Scholars program for JD students and oversees the Georgetown Law Technology Review, an active and well-read student-run and faculty-advised publication, and it publishes white papers, policy briefs, and other products of its faculty, staff, and affiliate scholars’ research. It organizes and deepens Georgetown’s programming and curricular efforts in technology-related fields. It coordinates its activities with other Centers and Programs, including the Knight Georgetown Institute, the Center on Privacy and Technology, and the Center on National Security. The institute supports development of affiliated programming and works towards establishing Georgetown Law as a preeminent forum for discussion and study of technology-related legal and policy issues.

The Executive Director develops the structure and programming of the Institute for Technology Law and Policy; works to establish the Institute as a leading voice in and convener of discussions and debates about technology law and policy; spearheads the Institute’s fundraising and communications efforts; collaborates with faculty members to develop research programs and oversees implementation; advises faculty about funding, staffing, and space needs; represents the Institute in high-profile fora and events; builds and maintains connections with University cross-campus collaborations including the Technology & Society Initiative; helps recruit key staff; oversees the publication of research; and supervises the day-to-day functions of Institute staff, fellows, and students.

The Executive Director oversees the Institute budget, including for staff salary, programs, and activities; and facilitates the administration of grant funding on behalf of principal investigators who are affiliated with the Institute.

The Executive Director’s work and duties may require occasional travel.

As AI Transformation Director, Marketing, you will set and drive marketing's AI adoption strategy and decide where AI can create the most value for marketing, then making sure those ideas become solutions people use. This is a strategy-and-delivery role: you'll prioritize where to invest, choose the right internal and external partners to build with, and stay close enough to execution to make sure what ships solves the problem and gets adopted. The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Job Overview
We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.

This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.

The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.

NFR is part of the Second Line of Defense providing independent oversight and challenge to management across compliance and operational risks. Non-Financial risks are managed at multiple levels (e.g., Firmwide, as well as Regional, Business Unit, Infrastructure Group, Control Function and Legal Entity).

The NFR Cyber, Technology and Information Security (CTIS) Department is focused specifically on managing cyber, technology and information security risks. The Center for Advancing Science and Technology (CAST) fuels innovation across physical sciences, engineering, computing, education, and policy to advance the nation’s future prosperity and resilience.
